- The are 2 main elevators for the 8-story building and one elevator didn’t work half the time and the other one is extremely slow
- The room is dark and outdated - the door in bathroom doesn’t close, the toilet doesn’t flush properly
- There’s leaks in the hallway ceilings here and there

Overall we had a great time but the quality of the building is not good.

reviews.author: Jason hanley
reviews.text: Beautiful ocean views and pools, our only 2 complaints were (1) food/drinks, plan on spending more for upgraded meals and drinks, all 45 people in our party would agree. (2) our concierge for the reserve side didn’t share the free things we get but have to book, daily pool cabana or hydrotherapy session at spa (spa was fabulous!)

reviews.author: Jimmie Estrada
reviews.text:
This hotel is absolutely gorgeous. The beach and pools are clean and nice and the service is mostly great. We had an issue with the shower and they sent someone up to fix it immediately.

My biggest complaint though was the food. The buffet was pretty bad. I’ve had better hospital food. The restaurants are very hit or miss. I really enjoyed Blue Agave but Capella was just okay and the place by the pool was probably one of the weirdest meals I’ve eaten at a restaurant. The sea bass was burnt and the mussels had some kind of Alfredo sauce drizzled on the shells.

Our room was pretty dated and the bed skirts had weird stains. One of the box springs was ripped and you could see it hanging down under the bed skirt. The bedding was not what I’d expect even for a 4 star hotel. Lumpy pillows/not plush mattress/sheets were standard threadcount.

I also had a weird interaction with a guest services staff member who misheard me when I told him my room number and then argued with me and said I gave him the wrong room number. He was not friendly and also gave me wrong information about my shuttle back to the airport and told me I’d have to pay for it and book it through one of the excursion desks in the lobby. Talked to someone else and it turns out that wasn’t true. The restaurant staff, bellhops, and housekeeping were very nice though.

I’d consider staying here again if the food was better but more than likely I’ll try somewhere else in the future.

reviews.author: Brigitte Gravelle
reviews.text:
The resort is beautiful and has a lot of potential. Food was great! Cabella was our favourite and Francisco and Dayvison were amazing servers!!!

If only all the other departments were as well staffed. The beach and pool areas were understaffed and lounge chairs were not available unless you went out before 6 am. There was 1 person for the entire resort for dinner reservations which led to having to wait in line for over 1.5 hrs only to be told nothing was available and we could only make reservations for 3 days at a time. We asked for a bottle opener on the first day we were here and never received it, and the bar fridge was not consistently restocked. The rooms are very dated.

reviews.author: Corina Settles
reviews.text:
This was our second time returning to Paradisus since our first time experience staying here was wonderful.

The room during our recent stay was not enjoyable, the air conditioning was not cool enough at night requiring us to request multiple times someone to assess the air conditioning. After multiple attempts, we were accompanied with a plug-in fan on the 2nd to last night that  helped with the room temperature enough.  The lighting function of the room was not up to par. The entry, living room and overhead bathroom sink lights were not working.

Roberto from the pool area was a wonderful service person and truly accommodated our requests as best possible every day during our stay. He is an extremely hard worker and would honestly return just for the sake of his service. Irina from the guest services bar was also very lovely, also Juan Manuel at the pool bar was excellent.

This resort is less than 20 minutes from the airport and they offer a taxi service to the airport for about $42 if needed.

reviews.author: Becky Cunning
reviews.text:
This was our second trip to Paradisus, the first trip being six years ago.  We have highly recommended this resort to many friends and family over the years.  However, this year was disappointing - not everything but enough that those are the things you remember.
First - Victor who is the pool concierge is AMAZING!!  5+ stars for Victor alone.  He is helpful, kind, fun, and goes above and beyond!  We enjoyed working and visiting with him.
Moises and Javier at the pool always took good care of us without any hesitation - they get five stars as well.
Our hotel concierge, Lily, was hardly seen and certainly didn't go out of her to make things easy as a five star hotel should.  Her sending us the activity list for the day at 3:00pm served no purpose at that point of the day.  We saw many others coming out and checking on their guest.  In our party of five, I personally saw her one time. Lily does not get five stars.
The pool was usually dirty, or dirtier than it should have been.  We were in the adult only pool, so should see a little less filth, than that of sharing with multiple families.  We saw them cleaning the pool, but would never keep the water above the skimmers in order for the pool itself to keep up with some of the problems.  This was in the adult pool and in the small "tanning pool".
The rooms were very disappointing, enough so that we moved room once and still wanted to a second time.
The air conditioning was not working well at all, in either room.
It was already not working well and then when housekeeping or turn down service would come in, they would turn the air conditioning OFF.  We would come back in at night ready for bed and have to deal with a hot room.  I was not happy about that.
The cleaning service did a mediocre job.  With sand, you would think that the floors would be swept daily.  They may have done part of the room, but I know for a fact it was not done completely every day.  Our bathroom counter was never wiped down, unless I did it.  The towel service was very sporadic and even then, they felt very cheap, crusty towels.  Not 4.5 quality star grade of linens.  The overall repair of the room was very poor, things were painted over instead of repaired or replaced.  The bottom of the door and door frame to the bathroom were wood rotted, the door wouldn't remain closed.  We saw a lot of building maintenance that needed repaired, not painted.  The indoor common areas were always hot and not enjoyable to spend time in due to the heat/humidity.
The in-room snacks and drinks were only stocked once.
Room service, food was cold when it got there.
Most of the restaurant food was ok, nothing amazing, other than the Steak House.
Steak House - definitely 5 stars.  Food was amazing and service was fantastic.
Overall, disappointed from our first experience.  It is not the worst place you will ever stay and you have several staff members that make up for a lot of the inadequacies, but doubt we will be returning due to this stay.  It was a much different experience from the first time.

reviews.author: Phil Gibson
reviews.text:
Hydrotherapy was incredible.  Felt good and Martin was helpful and provided insight for each step.
UPDATE: I wanted to provide an update on our stay at Paradisus Cancun.  As referenced above the spa experience was great, staff and massage therapist were excellent.  Ran into an issue with my locker and they resolved without incident.  Our room looked out over the ocean and pool area, which was great.  Service to rooms was excellent and rooms were clean and well kept.  The remaining staff at this location are very good and always friendly.
Now for the cons - This hotel is going to be closing in May for renovations, which are evident and needed.  We knew that going in, but decided to stay here anyway.   First issue, when booking if not booking through the hotel itself you are not guaranteed your room type(king/queen bed(s)) so my wife and I ended up with 2 double beds.  Not the end of the world, but not expected either because we were told we had a king at checkin.   Check in staff was less than helpful to resolve that situation, so started off vacation a bit irritated.  Secondly, due to short staffing the restaurant reservation system is a joke.  They act like they have all this availability, but allow people to book reservations for their entire stay and some people we heard were booking multiple reservations on the same day for different restaurants so they could decide what they wanted last minute.  All restaurants appeared to be half empty and in most cases you weren't able to walk up and possibly take a table that no one was using.  Half way through the stay, the staff finally admitted they were short staffed.  If you were willing to pay additional amount you could get a table...found that out later.  This system needs a full revamp.  We have stayed at other resorts in Cancun and the restaurant situation was much more suitable based on size of resort.  This hotel due to their upcoming closure just didn't have the staff to manage a full hotel of guests inside their restaurants.   Blue Agave, great tacos and staff was excellent.  Buffet food quality was average, selection very good.  Lemon Fish, average food, service good.  Sate, food good, service good, 3/4 empty when they said they were full.  We only were able to get a reservation here because we showed interest in a new program they were offering.   Reservation got screwed up a Flora, but manager was able to squeeze us in at last minute around 9pm, food below average and cold, service ok.  Didn't try the other restaurants due to reservation or availability challenges.

My guess is after renovations this will be a good place to try if they make appropriate changes to restaurants, staff increases and quality.  Just needs a refresh.   Be aware of possible room changes if you didn't book with hotel.  Overall a 3, but might be worth a try after reno.

reviews.author: laura saldana
reviews.text:
The hotel was understaffed for the amount of guests. This caused service to be very disappointing. The food was not good except at some of the restaurants. The buffet had good selection on New Year’s Eve but, usually fell short of tasty food on regular days. Dinner for New Year’s eve at one of the restaurants was a disaster! Waited close to two hours to get cold food and our server was rude since we got seated. Ended up eating at the buffet after.
Getting lounge chairs at beach and pool was impossible unless you get there at 7am to leave your belongings and hold up the space. People leave towels and stuff and don’t show up for hours or leave and don’t take their stuff and never return. Beds at beach aren’t exactly part of hotel. They belong to the Kanna Beach club and their prices ranged between $250-$500 per day depending on the day. That was very disappointing as they take up a very large area of beach front space that could be accessible for hotel guests as in having more “included” lounge chairs. New Year’s Eve event was not included with our “All-Inclusive” plan. Service at the event was surprisingly good and the experience was very pleasant. I’m glad we decided to pay extra for it. We enjoyed our stay because of the beautiful beach however, I would not visit this hotel again during high season. Needs more staff and better service during the Holidays.

reviews.author: Yann Audet
reviews.text: At the Flora restaurant, service by Anabel was really good. She was attentionate and really professionnal. The ambiance is also really good. However, the tuna tartar was extremely bad, it was shredded meat andtasteless. Truly a crime to the fish. The tandoori chicken was also bland and did not taste like much. The prawn with pumpkin risotto tasted like smoked pumpkin and nothing else. The duck was overcooked and rubbery. The soups were really good. Again Anabel did a really good job, the food was just not up to par.

reviews.author: Brooke Sweeney
reviews.text:
Paradisus Cancun – A Mixed Experience at a Beautiful Resort
My family and I recently returned from a stay at Paradisus Cancun, and I wanted to share an honest review of our experience. First and foremost, we’re incredibly grateful to have had the opportunity to go on a vacation and enjoy an all-inclusive resort. We realize that many of our disappointments are minor in the grand scheme of things. However, when staying at a resort that markets itself as a luxury destination, expectations are naturally higher—and in this case, many of those expectations were not met.
We were a group of five—four adults and one toddler—with two members having stayed at Paradisus properties more than five times. So, we came in with excitement and a sense of familiarity with the brand.
Highlights:
•	The beach was absolutely beautiful and one of the resort’s best features.
•	The food was quite good for an all-inclusive—definitely a positive.
•	The included sunset cruise that came with the concierge upgrade was a standout experience.
•	Evening shows and poolside entertainment were enjoyable and well-executed.
•	The massages we received at the spa were truly exceptional—some of the best we've ever had, and a real highlight of the trip.
•	Rosanna, one of the concierges, was a bright spot in our experience. She was kind, thoughtful, and went out of her way to make our stay special—especially for our toddler, leaving little gifts that made a big impression.
Areas of Disappointment:
Service:
Unfortunately, the service was inconsistent and often disappointing. While I understand the resort may have been understaffed due to an upcoming closure, the larger issue was not delays—it was the overall attitude of the staff. Many seemed unhappy or disengaged, and we felt more like a burden than a welcomed guest.
We upgraded to the concierge package, which turned out to be a poor value. We didn’t meet our assigned concierge, Galdino, until the final day—and only because we encountered an issue. That brings me to the biggest frustration: pool and beach daybeds.
Daybed Policy and Experience:
We used a daybed every day of our 6-day stay, only to be told on the final day that we were no longer allowed to reserve one. Suddenly, we were informed that the concierge upgrade only allows one daybed per room per stay—something we were never told at check-in. To make matters worse, there were multiple empty daybeds at the pool, and beach-facing beds were entirely vacant. Yet, they were asking $300 to reserve one. Frankly, that felt outrageous.
At a resort that claims to offer a luxury experience, this was a major letdown. A more thoughtful approach—such as offering complimentary access to loyal returning guests or reducing the rental cost—could have turned this into a memorable perk rather than a source of frustration.
Eventually, we were granted access to one of the unused daybeds, but only after considerable back and forth. It shouldn't have required that level of effort.
Final Thoughts:
The resort itself is beautiful, though it could use some updating in certain areas. The entertainment and setting provided some great moments, and the concierge sunset cruise was a real highlight. That said, the service experience and inconsistent policies left us disappointed—especially given the premium pricing.
We truly hope to see Paradisus return to the level of quality and service we’ve come to expect in the past. Until then, we’ll likely look elsewhere for future vacations.

reviews.author: Angela
reviews.text: The service at the resort was exceptional—attentive and friendly throughout our stay. However, the food was underwhelming. The buffet dishes were rarely warm, even right after opening, so you're better off dining at the resort’s restaurants for somewhat warmer and decent options but I would personally recommend eating at places outside the resort. We also encountered several cockroaches both inside and outside our room. Our room's lights were also flickering from the lamps to the ceiling lights in the bathroom. If you're interested in booking excursions, I recommend doing so through the Aquaworld booths at the resort; they offer a better deal, with the possibility of doing two or more excursions for the price of one compared to the desk inside the resort.

reviews.author: Meresiet Kidane
reviews.text:
We just recently stayed at the Paradisus Cancun. Overall, we had a great time, and we enjoyed the beautiful beach and the pool. The issue started when we checked into the hotel. We had reservations for two rooms/five nights. One of the rooms (3216) had a horrible, strong smell —it smelled like ammonia and bleach. We tolerated it the first night but couldn't take anymore, so I went to the front desk to address it. I was told by Cecelia (who she reported as one of the managers) that they would upgrade us at no cost. The issue was that there was no availability, and I had to return the next day before 10 am to complete the paperwork. I returned the next day and spoke with Enrique, who appeared not to care about the situation. He went back into a room and spoke to her, and she could not bother to come out to speak to me until I demanded that she come out. Then, I was informed that the room was not available as the guest had extended their stay. Then I was advised that there would be room available the next day and someone would reach out by 3 pm via text the next day. Surprise..surprise, no one reached out, and I had to go to the front desk and inquire. The same day, we find a giant roach in room 3216. I went to the front desk again, and later that afternoon, we saw maintenance spraying bug spray, and they indicated that the spray was not harmful.

Long story short, no one followed up about an upgrade or room change. No apologies were given.

This is by far unacceptable behavior from an alleged 5-star top-of-the-line resort. We spent thousands of dollars, and I spent an excessive amount of time speaking with the front desk instead of spending time with family. I strongly request that someone from Malia reach out ASAP to address some form of compensation. I will continue to post my grievances on every platform until someone reaches out and addresses this issue ASAP.

reviews.author: Tania G
reviews.text:
Edit: I added a star for location and added another star because on our last couple of days, the food got better in the buffet and the pool was less crowded but still completely full.

Honestly one of the worst all inclusive hotels we have ever been to! I do not recommend this hotel. The hotel is managed very poorly and is extremely overbooked and understaffed. You will spend 90% of your time waiting in line! There is a line up for everything including the buffet breakfast. If you want to secure a bed besides the beach or the pool, you have to wake up at 4 am and put a towel on the chair to take it. Even that is not guaranteed as other guests might move your towel. You have to have your breakfast by 7 AM if you want to avoid a line up. During your stay, you will see many FIGHTS over chairs! Also, you will hear EVERYONE talk about having to wake up early to secure their spot because there are not enough chairs. The hotel will try to sell you a “cabana” experience for $250 USD/day and will tell you guests are not allowed to put their towel on chairs and encourage you to move their towels. Do not do this, the HOTEL is responsible to ensure you have a good experience so do not get involved with other poor guests trying to get a spot! The reality is the hotel just want you buy the cabana and will not provide enough chairs for their guests.
Activities are scheduled but do not follow the scheduled times and begin 20-30 minutes late. There is spinning on the schedule but out of the 4 days we showed up to the gym, none had an instructor.
Shows are average and performed near the pool. There is no stage and guess what? YEP, no CHAIRS.  There are not enough seats. 60% of people have to stand up and watch the show.
Although the Food stands and restaurants during the day have operating hours, they randomly close 20-30 minutes before the schedule. Even if you are in the line, they won’t serve you and will tell you it is closed.
Don’t waste your hard earned money. Food is average to good here and you will hear many reviews focused on food. But you won’t be able to relax here, there is too much tension. The only upside is staff are nice and the beach is beautiful, if you don’t mind having no shade or chair!
Also, there is a shortage of towels and restocking is not consistent. Although housekeeping is very nice, they don’t have enough towels to give you.
You won’t be able to get bottled water near the pool or the beach and they don’t restock it in your room frequently. They look you in the eye and tell you bottled water is for “reserved” guests ONLY. There is no kettle in the room to boil water.
There is also a line up for elevators and although we personally did not mind taking the stairs, if you are on the upper floors (7 or 8 ) consider that as a warning. You have to line up and wait 10-15 min for elevators.
Another weird thing is food is not seasoned well and there is no salt and pepper on tables.

reviews.author: Ramandeep Dhadda
reviews.text: When I went with 3 children aged 6-8 on a family vacation. After travelling for almost 12 hours I reached the hotel and the receptionists who checked us in her name was Romina was very very rude and had no smile. No thank you or welcome. We travel to hotels a lot and this was the first time we had seen such a bad receptionists. We stayed for a week and one time while I was in shower and once when drying my hair the breaker went out. No electricity and no lights and no power. First time it took 15 mins to fix and second time more than 30mins. The phone number to room service was very disrupted and couldn’t hear anything. The restaurant waiters however were very good especially Armando. Can not say for Romina. The floor was leaking in the floor outside our room and there was water everywhere but no signs saying to be careful or there is slippery floor.

reviews.author: Sherry L
reviews.text: Beautiful resort, however I did find the service to be lacking.  Quiet, so if you're looking for a party this isn't the place. Not "exciting" but very relaxing. Pools close early, 6pm I believe which is too early. Beach is beautiful. Hard to find seating as all pool chairs get claimed usually before 8am if it's going to be a sunny day.

reviews.author: María Inés Parnisari
reviews.text:
The good: amazing architecture, the staff was super friendly and accommodating, food was plentiful, I had fun at the karaoke bar and the silent disco. There is a shop inside the resort for essential items (eg sunscreen)

The bad: my stomach didn't like either the food or the water, I had diarrhea for three days while I was in the hotel (and I didn't leave it). My room (1609) had poor lighting when taking a shower, and I couldn't figure out how to shut off the pipe that fills the tub. The layout is a bit inconvenient, to get to my room I had to walk towards the very last elevator, and there is only one elevator per pyramid.

reviews.author: Carlos Mesquita
reviews.text: The Acqua Marina restaurant is absolutely fantastic! The food is exceptional, the service is impeccable, and the atmosphere provides a unique and welcoming experience. I want to highlight the outstanding service from Carlos, Jaime, Chef Erik, and Martin, who were truly amazing. Every detail was handled with care and professionalism. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Gustavo Gonzalez
reviews.text: We had a great time at the pool! Our designated spot was at a table right infront of mascalzone. Daniel made us the best pizza. He’s very friendly and inviting and quick with the pizza. This place does get crowded and he handled it well! While we lounged in the pool Irina came to check on us and restock our drinks multiple times. It shows she didn’t forget about us! She would made us feel at home, she’s the best at supplying your drinks and making sure nothing is missing for you. Great service and our designated lunch spot the whole time we stayed!

reviews.author: Brenda Winebrenner
reviews.text: Looks like we had a fabulous day thanks to the staff, reservations were not clear. We were requested a two bedroom suite and ended up with a one bedroom suite for four people. We were told we needed to contact Corporate to correct this. Being on vacation, we wanted something stress-free and thanks to the service folks. They were awesome, eating breakfast and receiving service from Ignacio Vasquez ,Martin Ku and Martin Arzeto started our days. Our housekeepers were outstanding. There needs to be better communication with reservations, but we will come back and give them another chance. The service Folks, has been what is made our stay here so memorable.

reviews.author: Bren A
reviews.text: Good experience at Paradisus Cancun, however rooms and overall resort is showing a lot of aging and wear. Buckets and towels often seen around due to leaks, rooms could definitely use a renovation. Service is 10/10, wonderful, attentive and friendly staff. Food and drinks are great as well. Only criticisms are the actual state of the resort and rooms needing renovations and added cleanliness. We saw a few bugs at times.  Overall, had a wonderful time due to the beautiful beach, pools, and incredible staff, but would not come back unless it were renovated.

reviews.author: Skyler Havlik
reviews.text: We had a great family vacation here in the reserve section! George was our concierge and exceeded all of our expectations. He was so helpful and nice. The A/C needs help, 3/4 rooms had problems. The food was really good, highly recommend Lemon Fish. The beach was perfect, crystal clear water with fun waves. If you are looking for a party hotel this is not it. Minimum night time entertainment, but we enjoyed relaxing. Also, one of our groups room they found two roaches!

reviews.author: Soniya Mehta
reviews.text: Electricity was off for one entire day and we were not notified about this until the day before. Air conditioner was supposed to start working at 6pm as stated on the notification, but never turned back on in our room. We were told by multiple staff that it would take “15 more minutes” for it turn on again. By 11pm we had spoke with 6 different staff members and I was still sweating profusely in my own room. Guest services refused to change our room, until we asked to speak with management. Finally around 12pm midnight they switched us to a room with working air conditioning. On this day was my birthday and I planned for this ahead of time to be my resort day. This experience really ruined it for me because I wasted my day trying to get a room with AC. Also, nothing special was done for me on my birthday. I read other reviews and saw photos of this resort placing something in the rooms to celebrate birthdays, but nothing was done for me. Also, there were very minimal vegetarian options in all of the restaurants. If you are a vegetarian, I would not recommend this resort at all!  Lemon Fish was the only restaurant I was able to have a satisfying meal at. Beautiful resort and great view of the ocean, but I would never stay here again.

reviews.author: Omar Luna
reviews.text: The staff at the Blue Agave were amazing, Atilano and Perla our servers were very attentive and provide us with the best service, the food was also good. Servers and staff by the pool area and other restaurants were also great. We have stayed at this hotel 3 other times and this has been the 1st time we have experienced the power going out 3 times for several hours. The first being the night we arrived not a very good impression, we decided we would give it another try and 3 days later in it happened again. When I went to guest services all they could tell me was they were sorry for the inconvenience and that they didn't have an time for the restoration unacceptable. The Lagoon view rooms need some updating. We decided to upgrade our room to ocean view, the room had been updated and was more bright and inviting.

reviews.author: Marco Valdez
reviews.text:
We stayed for 5 days 4 nights at the Paradisus hotel recently for our anniversary.

Once we arrived we were greeted excellently and was in awe of the beautiful decor and smell from the plants. We were also greeted with drinks and were given a tour of the hotel  and restaurants.

We decided to eat before heading to our  room and went with the Blue Agave Restaurant. Beautifully designed and were excited for our 1st meal at this resort. We were then attended to and our waitress did not seem to be having a good day. She then proceeded to take our order and then went to the back and  started throwing dishes and glasses on table. We could see her and she knew it as well, only her attitude seem to change when one of the waiters came in and hugged her.

We proceeded to our room which was beautifully designed and had an amazing view of the lagoon. Temperature in the room was perfect.

That being said we thought that the next few days would be perfect, but this was not the case. That night we went back to our room for bed and went to sleep.

The air conditioner stopped working, half of the outlets stopped working.

We called the front desk and notified them of this and maintenance man came in and said that the air conditioner stopped working because it was not running and caused the outage for the outlets.

This went on for the entire stay, we decided to enjoy the rest of our stay and not let it bother us.

Luis, Miguel and Diana were excellent bartenders and went the extra mile for us would highly recommend them.

We are planning to return back to Cancun and hopefully will not have the same experience with the rooms.

reviews.author: Sonia
reviews.text:
3.5/5 Stars. This is our third time in Cancun and first stay here.

PROS: Amazing service. Cannot say enough good things about the staff. From the moment you arrive, someone welcomes you, takes you to the check-in desk. All servers from the pool area to the restaurant are super nice.

Beach is wide and a beautiful blue, sandy white beach. Waves were rough but that's not the hotels fault.

Beautiful property. The lobby is gorgeous, beautiful decor throughout.

Food was pretty good for the most part. The Al A Carte restaurants were just okay. Portion sizes were pretty small. We tried Lemon Fish, Cielo and Sante. Sante was probably the best one and it's oceanside. Buffet was good but lacked the variety from other AIs I've experienced in the past.

Pool side food service was great though.

CONS:

The hotel has too many guests and not enough chairs. I had to wake up at 6am to get chairs. After 7am, forget about getting a spot at the pool or beach. Saw many frustrated people.

The rooms are falling apart. Our shower drain was clogged and the mini fridge leaked. Staff are quick to come to the room and patch things up but the rooms are in need of repair.

Entertainment is so so. There are "shows" outside each night but they are small productions and not like the grand shows I've experienced at most AI resorts over the years.

reviews.author: Juan Carlos Castro
reviews.text:
We were excited for a relaxing getaway the week before Thanksgiving, but unfortunately, this hotel fell short of our expectations for a 5-star experience.  While the room was a decent size, it showed signs of wear and tear with worn carpets and dated decor.  Every time we showered, a huge puddle would form by the toilet, which was a real inconvenience.  We were also surprised that the TVs weren't smart TVs, limiting our entertainment options.

The buffet was acceptable, but the à la carte restaurants were disappointing. We were especially let down by the Japanese restaurant. Despite its beautiful setting, the food was subpar (sushi rolls, ceviche, and aguachile were all pretty tasteless). We actually ended up going to the buffet afterward because we were still hungry and we did not want to get anything else from that restaurant.

Even though we visited during the low season, finding a beach chair by the pool or beach was a challenge. We often had to wait for over an hour in the late morning to find available chairs.  The "Balinenses" beds looked amazing, but the $250 USD price tag was exorbitant, especially considering it was more than the cost of our nightly stay!

We paid approximately $190 USD per person per night for a triple room, which seemed like a great deal for a 5-star all-inclusive. However, the overall experience felt more like a 3.5 or 4-star hotel with limited inclusions. To truly enjoy the resort, we would have had to pay extra for many amenities, which would likely be even more necessary during the high season.

While we enjoyed spending time together, we were ultimately disappointed with this hotel and wouldn't return. Next time, we'll explore other resorts in the area that offer better value and amenities.

reviews.author: Homer Zehtabi
reviews.text:
I'd give this place 3 stars.
PROS:
- Close to the airport
- Staff except for 1 or 2 are very polite and helpful
- Even sales staff at the sales office were polite, helpful and not pushy
- Architecture is absolutely beautiful
- Facilities are mostly clean

CONS:
- The food quality needs improvement. Not that it's bad but it is nowhere close to most 5 star hotels I've tried in Cancun
- Somehow everyday, they ran out of things. Lemon, Avocado, Salt (I'm not kidding), Burger and more
- Rooms are quite old and need update. There are some rooms that are not even at a quality of a 2 star level. It was so bad that we walked in and right back out. The staff were kind enough to change the room but that kind of room should not be given to anybody.
- On a rainy day, there's absolutely nothing to be done at the hotel and they don't seem to plan ahead to keep those days full of activities. They only had 3 or 4 activities all day.
- Anything you purchase at the hotel stores are easily between 5-10 times more expensive than what you can buy in Canada or the U.S.

Overall I would say this hotel would not have a 5 star reputation was it not for an absolutely incredible staff.

reviews.author: Yiv K
reviews.text:
Had a nice time but please believe the bad reviews too. For families and people who want to relax — December 2024 with 2 adults, 3 kids. Slept in Pyramid 3, we purchased the all-inclusive for 7 days.

1.) HOTEL- Visually beautiful and well maintained 2.) ROOM- First day the fridge was not working, we requested it to be fix, never fixed. Water leaking on the washroom floor. The closet door broke, and we had to call to fix it. We had 2 cockroaches in the room, killing only 1 — YES, very noisy can hear everything. People talking while walking by, the night music from the entertainment, fireworks and our room was by the fountain (loud fountain). We requested no Pyramid Three but still gave us Pyramid Three 3.) FOOD- Service is top notch, so please tip. Food decent but something is missing, lacking taste. Other places in Mexico have better. Favourite spot was Aqua Marina — you eat there at lunch, it opens  at 1:15PM, no reservation. Dinner, you need a reservation, dinner team thank you so much, they are fantastic! Reservations for dinner restaurants begins at 10AM. YES, there will be a wait line. We highly recommend booking all dinners. Dinner restaurants don’t show kids menus but they have a menu, ask the server for the options 4.) POOLS- Large, beautiful and can be deep for non-swimmers or short individuals. Deep areas are about 5’5 feet and edges can be 4’feet. There is a kids area, no slides, just a rectangle pool area, about 2’feet and 1 kids circle pool for toddlers. Servers at the pools, so kind and caring. They always come to see if you need anything (drinks and food). Thank you for your hard work, it really shows! Be very careful of Pizza by the pool. We ate a lot of it. Near the end of lunch-service there was no one at the station. A bunch of birds were eating the ingredients and sitting on the counter top, where they literally made the pizza. Birds were comfortable doing that, so it is probably the birds routine. Try to eat pizza at the beginning of lunch service 5.) POOL SEATS/TOWELS- There is no towel card system. You will see towels everywhere. We learned the hard way. You have to wake up at 6AM to put your towel on your spot and put a personal item (sunglasses, book, shirt, water container). First day we did not put a personal item on our spot. When we came back, someone took our spot. We asked for our spot because we woke at 6AM to put our towels on the seats but they did not move. If you have no personal item on your spot, people will assume it is available, they will move your towel off and take your spot 6.) BALI BEDS- It is $250 USD a day. If you are a CIRCLE member it is cheaper. You can get it for free, for one day if you go to the CIRCLE meeting. Which can take 2 hours of your day or if you do an upgrade— When we were there, a representative did offer $50 USD. So it depends on the person 7.) BEACH- Wonderful, very clean, the water is so blue and warm. Sand is super soft and pretty. Be careful, strong waves and not able to swim in. Shout out to the servers on the beach! You are super, I would be tired going up and down carrying many drinks and food! Especially on a hot day!!!

Visually appealing but not our best experience.

reviews.author: Olga Alekseeva
reviews.text:
Disappointed. For $900 a night we got a room right next to the bar, so we couldn’t sleep till 1-2am as the room was shaking. Non reclining sun beds. Soft nice beds at the beach and pool cost 250. Food is great. You can’t reserve table at the restaurant so you have to go there and then wait 1 hour to get a table. No fun evening entertainment, only very loud singing that makes you go outside. Too loud in the hotel.
Lagoon view rooms are terrible. We upgraded to ocean view. Why do we get a concierge? He is only trying to sell you membership and waste your time. The beach is good.

reviews.author: M Scott Martin
reviews.text:
We booked a 7-night stay over Christmas at Paradisus Cancún, a Meliá hotel. It’s hard to describe how disappointed we were. We booked a “Premium Suite Lagoon View” room which was pricey – and we booked it more than 8 months early. What we got was a first-floor room in the timeshare section with a view of the hallway doors that lead to the pool area. It wasn’t even on the correct side of the building. The bedroom flooded when it rained, the kitchen fan made a noise so loud it couldn’t be used, and the bathroom sink drained slowly.

The reservation desk just said that room types aren’t guaranteed and that no other rooms were available. We even offered to have our room downgraded. We asked for a manager and were taken to guest services instead. They offered to give us access to the spa for a day – not spa services, just access to the spa (sauna, etc.).

This was the beginning of a very discouraging stay at Paradisus Cancun. We had the all-inclusive package but found out that in order to have dinner at any of the included restaurants, you had to book them between 10AM and 4PM, a time when most people are on excursions. And the reservation desk usually had a very long line. So, we were forced to eat our first 2 dinners at the buffet, which is mediocre at best. Their coffee was weak.

We finally were at the hotel 1 day between 10-4 & were able to make dinner reservations for the rest of the stay.  We found Sante, Aqua Marina, and Flora to be excellent restaurants.  However, the house white wine included in the price wasn’t drinkable and the red was very low-end. We had Christmas dinner at Capella, and this was worse than the buffet. The food looked like it had been warmed over from days before. Thankfully the live Christmas show that was blasting into the restaurant got rained out halfway through dinner and our group could finally talk.

The other 3 rooms booked for family members were better – the only complaint was lack of hot water. Several times it was tepid and one time it was cold.

We did enjoy the grounds, the pools and the beach and the staff was pleasant. The hotel has great potential. If you have a decent room with a view, you will likely have a better experience than we did.

One other note: for tipping, take lots of smaller bills in pesos with you as we couldn’t get change anywhere at the hotel.

reviews.author: Anusha
reviews.text: This is an all inclusive resort. It has it's own advantages and disadvantages. Once you enter the place you don't have to pay for anything. Depending on your reservation class, you can enjoy the facilities accordingly. There are so many options to enjoy. Food , entertainment, bar and so on. But the worst part for us was the reception and the type of room we got. As a couple we expect to get at least a single queen  size bed. But they were not able to help us with the same. We as a couple ended up sleeping in 2 separate beds. The reception was so rude. I need to tell the name of Mr Rafael who was very rude and was in his own world when we tried to explain our problems. He had his own readymade answers rather than giving solutions to our issues. He completely ignores you. So be sure not to get served from Rafael in the reception .

reviews.author: Frosty Jack
reviews.text:
Our room was ok (Sunset view), but to be fair we booked it at the last minute as a pivot from a hotel that’s currently getting terrible reviews, so we get what we get. The food was pretty good, better than most all-inclusives we’ve stayed at over the years. The service was excellent most of the time. The real problems showed when the hotel was full, they just aren’t equipped to handle that volume of guests. Leading up to Christmas, things were crowded, but not terribly so. Three days after Christmas, things got crazy busy and you were lucky to get any service by the pool. One pretty major annoyance is the nightclub across the street. If you’re booked on the Sunset side, expect to hear their base thumping until 4am. Clearly the hotel can’t do much about this, but it’s something to seriously consider before booking this place. All in all, it’s not a bad hotel. It’s a little dated, but you’ll see maintenance people running around daily doing paint touch ups, patching, and repairs to try and keep things looking fresh. The gym was nice, it’s not often you get well maintained and solid treadmills to jog on at a hotel.

Another point of frustration was getting the room cleaned. This seemed to be hit or miss and it varied when maid service would get to your room. My best guess is this was a symptom of the hotel being full but not staffed to accommodate.

We also didn’t have hot water for one day, but in reading some of the other reviews, we were lucky.

To add, you’ll benefit greatly by being an early riser here. Get up early to reserve a good spot by the pool or beach (5:00am), get to the buffet before 8:30am, try to reserve your evening meals the day you get there (reservation times fill up). If you wait, you’ll be stuck in long lines and you’ll never get a spot poolside. Is it irritating? Absolutely, but that’s just how the game is played at a lot of these resorts.

But, like I said before, the service was excellent! Shout out to Odon at Cielo, and Martin, Cande, and Manuel at Malva! All of the hotel staff we interacted with ranged from dutiful to friendly, and none of them were rude or impolite.

reviews.author: Anita karadjian
reviews.text:
Jan 3rd was our arrived date, we always look at reviews and Im so lost as everything look great ! arrival took for ever , we booked in September , I booked a double bed paid extra for ocean ! oh boy ! we got a room looked like 90's cod bed for my kid , old nasty, paint on mirrors and more .next day we receive our double bed ( end of the day )in the basement with partial view!!!! , so disappointed, complained there excuse was they have a convention , how is this my problem we paid top dollar like everyone else. nothing for kids ( not even pool inflated balloon like advertised ), we kept Lemon fish resto for last because apparently was the best  , we received cold noodles , everything we tried to order was no longer available , service was slow ! the resto outside was better ,Nespresso bar was the only good thing , and Ginger bar staff was amazing ! your show last 45 min every night , in the ginger 2 is where there's action dj ect , BUT you freeze in there, and mostly teenagers.Beach beautiful, service in beach you need franseco !
they are renovation in March !! would have been nice to know !
lets just say we had a lady taking everyone emails to complain , no need to say more , if you already  booked make sure you are not in phase 1 that's where everything is older. I'm truly disappointed as the resort is beautiful inside. And front desk people not so welcoming , Hotel guest service was better service ! oh and room service after 2 orders , they will charge you for service fee!! and food limited and you wait 45 min ! maybe after renovations it will be better , but nothing was OFFERED for our troubles. NOTHING 2 days of anger , they could care less.

reviews.author: Rachel Bostron
reviews.text: My experience at Paradisus was just decent. I say this only because we paid extra for The Reserve and I have never experienced such disorganization and would expect better service since being in the Reserve is suppose to provide a higher tier experience. My "concierge" although very friendly never sent me schedules or information about most things she said she was going too. She basically booked two dinners for me which I would of rather done myself. Also the stay is suppose to include Sals steak house which was too full so I never got to have dinner there, 2 FULL bali bed days which I was waitlisted for, thank god people did not show up or else we only had a reservation for one full day which was the day we were leaving. The first night we arrived we were forced to eat at the buffet because no one told us that we needed to book dinner reservations or helped us do that, apparently concierge is suppose to reach out before your trip and set you up for that night with reservations. I also had to book my own transportation to and from the hotel which with other resorts this is not the case. The service people were always nice, but never memorable. The food was edible but most things lacked salt and flavor, absolutely not the food id would expect at a "5 star" resort the only food we really enjoyed was dinner at the specialty restaurants. It seemed this place was very short on staff alot of times there were lines with only one person working at a station. Restaurants were all "full" but yet all the seats were empty. It was odd. The rooms are a little outdated water leaked all over the floor because the shower door didnt close all the way and the air conditioner ran 24/7 and was very loud and most of the outlets near the bed did not work. Nightly and even day activities were sparse and everything is closed right before 11, so if you are a person who likes to do things an have experiences dont count on this resort to provide that. And then upon checking out concierge said they would reserve a changing room at 3pm before our picking up at 4pm. When I went to guest services to tell them about the changing room they said "Oh they are full" so whats the point of the reservation? Really none of it made sense. Although its a beautiful resort, and the cleaners are very good btw, I would not stay again and definitely would not pay extra to be a reserve guest since everything included pretty much was not.

reviews.author: Jan Ouano
reviews.text:
Our trip to Paradisus Cancun had its good and not-so-good moments. Right when we got there, a bunch of friendly hotel staff came up to us. They seemed nice at first, chatting and offering us free spa treatments or a day on a fancy beach bed. But, it was all a setup to get us into a meeting about joining their club, CIRCLE by Melia. They said it'd be quick, like 30 minutes to an hour tops, but it dragged on for almost four hours! My partner and I were so tired and fed up that we ended up signing up just to end it. Later, I did some reading and found out more about it, and canceled it the next day. Again, this is an hour of me reading reviews instead of enjoying my holiday. Getting our money back took over a month, though.

That whole sales pitch thing was a big downer. It took a big chunk out of our vacation time, which was really annoying. I guess we should've just said no from the start, but they were so persuasive, and we got caught up in the moment. Kudos to the Melia sales strategy though, catching customers in their happy holiday mood, and pitching a holiday membership can make them listen in to the pitch. But it's unsustainable as once customers do their due diligence, they end up finding ways to cancel.

But it wasn't all bad. The people working at the hotel were actually amazing. The folks at the buffet and the pool bar were super nice and always made sure we had everything we wanted. They really appreciated any tips, and being a bit more generous with them went a long way. The food was pretty good overall, especially at this sushi place, Lemon Fish – that was top-notch. Everyone from the cleaning crew to security was friendly and made our stay nicer.

So, yeah, if we ever go back, we'll know to steer clear of those sales meetings and just enjoy the good stuff.

reviews.author: Kevin H
reviews.text:
Overall, the resort met our expectations, which were set somewhat lower from reading previous reviews.  The staff went above and beyond and everyone was pleasant.  We got a good last minute price, so it would have been disappointing if we had paid more.

Check-in: fast, efficient, no drama.

Restaurants:  Sal steakhouse was good, Atrium restaurant had the best deserts, chocolates, and treats.  Buffet was just ok (parents need to monitor both children and grand-parents who seemed to like to handle food, then put it back!). Nespresso coffee bar in the lobby was great.

Pool:  Reserve pool was excellent, Nicole was awesome, we reserved Bali beds for a couple days - you must do this at the pool as soon as you arrive , the concierge does not look after this.

Bars:  Pool bar was great, had some top shelf offerings that were available if you asked.  There were some cocktails that you had to pay extra which is frustrating at an all-inclusive.

reviews.author: Vivek Shah
reviews.text:
The overall feel in the resort is good because of how big the central open area is with beautiful scenery. Plenty of restaurants all around the property. Some of the bartenders are great. That's pretty much where the good things end.

We were 9 families and every single family spent a good amount of time checking into the hotel because of how slow the staff was. Some of the families had bad rooms with leaking sinks, etc. We encountered overworked workers all around the property who would get irritated if we asked for silverware type stuff. It was clear that the staff only cared for tips and if you didn't tip them "Every single time" you got service from them, you were bound to get poor service the following time.
We asked for mango that was not frequently restocked during breakfast and we were asked to pay for it!! Really??
The central open area had loud music right from the morning and was disturbing if you were staying on lower levels. The club across the street was extremely loud and would play music until 5am. Not the hotel's fault but it'll disturb your sleep. The food seemed lavish but the taste was average at best in Malva bazaar.
Was it a 5 star feeling?? Not exactly. Was it a good property? Yes. Will I recommend it to others? If you find another 5 star property for similar price, I would say no.

reviews.author: Francisco Bianchi
reviews.text:
This is far from a 5 stars hotel!
It is a "OK" customer service, rooms are very outdates, very old looking.
We had no hot water on 3rd day, 2 first days we had nothing on mini fridge and no snack as they said we would have!
They are "all inclusive", you dont have all included!
You need to fight for chairs by the pool, no chair at all by the beach, unless you pay a very high price for it (if you get luck to find availability).
We had no information that the reserve was only for special member and literaly got kicked out of there when we got in because lack of information.
They took 2 hours trying to sell us their membership but nobody took any second to make sure our needs werw beeing taken care of.
You get bored a lot because the only intertaiment is the pool, beach and restaurants that are always full and you have long waits to get a seat and your food.
Def not returning! Def not becoming a member!

reviews.author: H T
reviews.text:
The food is good with exception of few restaurants but overall its very good. The only thing is serving time at be extremely long in the restaurants depending on how busy they are.feel like they are somewhat short on staffs.

The room, the beach and the hotel amenities were really nice.

The check-in was rough. We did not get checked in until 4 when we arrived at 11am. The front desk staff are very unhelpful they just kept asking us to come back and line up again like there is nothing they can do.

Another major issue we had was with the concierge David that was assigned to us. During our stay we have been approached by many concierges to ask us about our stay and to listen to the membership presentations of the hotel. We declined most of them except one convinced us to go. Our concierge David got really upset with us for going to the hotel presentation without telling him and questioned us why. This was totally unexpected. We thought that all the staff was working together as a team for the hotel and why is it the guest problem to make sure we tell him when we go to the presentation. He wants an explanation from us and he said they don't work as team which I'm shocked. Later that day when we said hi to him he just ignored us. He stopped WhatsApping us or help us after that. I have never been treated this way by a hotel staff especially in a 5 star resort.

reviews.author: Sharada Rayan
reviews.text:
This place is optimized for the aesthetics. The food was very bad, even though it was plated nicely. The people working there was nice, it was beautifully decorated but If food is important to you on a vacation, do not go here.

Also I wouldn’t trust the reviews. After every meal, or experience, the staff will approach you with a QR code to leave the reviews so a majority of these reviews are probably bias.

reviews.author: hildaries1
reviews.text:
My family and I stayed at Paradisus from 6/10 - 6/13/2024. The hotel is beautiful, specifically the entrance, lobby, and restaurant areas. Unfortunately we didn’t encounter the same when it came to the accommodation/rooms. We had reservations for two rooms and had specified that my father would be using a wheelchair and had limited mobility. With that being said, we were placed on the first floor which was great, unfortunately the room was not great, the bathroom was in poor shape, the headboards were dusty and the furniture was outdated. In the other room, there was a piece of pipe that was missing from the bathroom sink 🤯!

Eventually we were able to speak with a manager and paid to upgrade our rooms, and they were better. Still not what we would expect but we didn’t want to keep on moving our things considering that we were traveling with 3 children and an adult with limited mobility.

The one thing I would like to highlight is the EXCELLENT service from the staff. From the reception area, maintenance, housekeeping, and waiters. I would like to call out Pascual, Candelario, and Gerardo from the Malva Food Bazaar; Pascual is the best! We spotted a table for about 10 people that we started sitting at for breakfast, by the third day, Pascual already had our 6 coffee cups set ready to go because he anticipated our arrival. Honestly, he made the experience so much better, gracias Pascual!

We also had a great experience at Flora, the food here was absolutely delicious!!! Our first night there we were greeted by our server Cynthia, the best!

Overall it was a good experience but could have been definitely great if we hadn’t encountered the maintenance or lack there of, of the rooms.

reviews.author: Shelonda Wilson
reviews.text:
UPDATED REVIEW:

The hotel agreed to refund me my $350 & I agreed to update the review noting that. This was the $350 they charged me to move to a room that with the specifications I booked. Room 2506 they originally put us in had a view of tower 1, not the lagoon and was severely outdated. The hotel admitted they should have never charged me. (I have not received my $350 yet and will update the post once I actually receive it). I departed the hotel on 7/13 and was told would take up to 10 days to process.

For the Pros and Cons:

Pros:
All of the service staff (in all the restaurants and poolside), bellhop, and the lady making the pizzas poolside. Dider, Hector, and everyone working the cabanas pool side. Oscar in sales and the sales team. Lastly, Alejandro in guest services.

Cons:
This place is definitely starting to look its age (40) especially tower 2. They have old & dated furniture and the tubs are hazardous. My aunt and mom had a very hard time getting in and out, they had 3 different rooms during our stay and they all had this very old bulky tub. They were in rooms 2119, then 2507, & finally 4019. 2119 had mold and a severe water leak (see pics), 2507 had a sensor issue which caused the lights to randomly go out, once while my mother was in the shower. 4019 the shower did not work for 2 days, finally guest services sent someone to show us “how to use the shower” only to discover both shower heads needed to be replaced (see video). There were also little bugs coming in from the balcony of 4019.

We were moved from 2506 to 4003 which had no hot or warm water. They worked for almost 2 hours to finally get us warm water and said it was bc ppl don’t typically use warm water here. After that the warm water was still sketchy and became nonexistent by the time we departed. Room 4003 also had drain flies(I had to google what they were). The furniture is outdated but the hotel said our room was upgraded (see pics).

Lastly this is not a kid friendly hotel, maybe for older kids 12+. All of the pools are 5 feet+, not safe for small kids at all. I am 5’5 and was mostly on my tippy toes the entire time with the exception of the bar area and sun shelf/tanning ledge. Most of the kids played on the tanning ledge which is not exactly a kids area. Also, Unless you bring your own toys the kids can only splash water. On Wednesday they did bring a blow up slide to the poolside for the kids. The cabanas are $250 per day and come with a bottle of Moët and one lobster tail. They should also offer the cabanas at $150 without the Moët and lobster tail. I had to pretty much drink the entire bottle myself bc no one else wanted it, the one lobster tail was good but we didn’t really eat the other sides.

I am giving this hotel 3 stars bc the service staff was amazing. Aqua Marina is very good, we enjoyed them for lunch and dinner. I did notice most of the 5 star reviews are from the guest in the Reserve, adult only side. I did get to see one of the rooms on that side and they are a lot better than tower 2.

reviews.author: SoCal Review
reviews.text: Older resort with pros and cons - mostly pros.  Service was excellent and everyone was very helpful.  The rooms and baths need updating.  But was comfortable as you cannot really hear next door neighbors.  Many events and activities available during the week.  Food options were good.

reviews.author: Jason Salameh
reviews.text:
Overall: Paradisus Cancún has tremendous potential but has a few areas they need to improve. 1/ more staff, clearly the staff are short handed, this meant long wait times and less than ideal services in general - eg 2-3 hours at a dinner table 2/ aging facilities, the place really needs some TLC - eg during a blight of rain, you will observe leaks everywhere. Eg, a/c water trays seem to overflow, causing leaks into rooms or damaged walls and mold. You can see them constantly patching up 3/ refreshed amenities, there were a few notable things missing such as restaurants, jacuzzi and proper kids play areas to name a few.

Room: checked into a grand master suite. The first room that We received had some issues. Paint was peeling off the ceiling. It seemed like there was a water leak somewhere above the room. We had to wait the night there while they exchange the room for us. We believe that this leak had been happening for some time as there was a little bit of mold

Concierge: Sergio was great. Very prompt to answer all our questions and help us find a new room when ours didnt work out. Also helped us book various venues and amenities throughout the property. Sergio made our stay great!!

Food: Great overall selection. Great restaurants. Great service.

Pool: overall, the pool is great. Water is a little bit on the cold side. I believe one critical amenity they are missing here would be a Jacuzzi.

Poolside service; Didier Was our server. He was continually prompt. Always checked in on us. Not only offered us exceptional service, But also was proactive to get us things before we even asked for them. He got to know the family, which is great. We really appreciated him. We were a large party of 11 people, and he came to know each one of us what we wanted

reviews.author: Fabio Cavagnolli
reviews.text: Right in the first day I founded a paint roller brush inside my room.  By the third day the AC started leaking and flooded the washroom. On the last day they had 2 weeding parties being hosted at the hotel simultaneously, one of them was taking place at the pool right in front my bedroom, the music was very loud and lasted till past midnight. I noticed that the services provided at the beach were different depending on the waiters, in the first 2 day it was excellent, but by the third day the waiters came up with different rules and were trying to charge extra for the same services that were free of charge on the previous days.

reviews.author: Maria Chkeri
reviews.text:
Service everywhere was extremely slow. I was not impressed with the rooms. They smelled moldy and stuffy.
I do want to recognize and give a huge Shout out to Carlos at the nespresso Cafe. He always served guests with a smile. He is such a hard worker and I appreciated his service.
Overall, our stay was nice. I most likely won't come back due to the subpar food quality and mold smell of rooms. However, I will be remiss to disregard the team's impressive customer service; most were really nice and welcoming.

reviews.author: Rod Mucio
reviews.text:
Paradisus Cancun is an OK resort compared to a number of places we've been in the Caribbean. The room is nice with a view at the lagoon.
The buffet lunch is mediocre, but breakfast is good. However, I ended up calling the waiter for water and coffee as nobody came, and it's been several minutes waiting for a service.
We tried the following restaurant: Celio- Mexican. Food and service are good.
Agave- taco place. Food and service are good too.
Capella-Italian, service was very good, and we find the food ok but salty.

Now, the resort has a huge garden area with flowing water inside the building. This open space has no air conditioning. You will have to go thru this area each time, and it's hot and humid.

Beach and pool area are nice, but the beach has no bar service.
Overall it was just ok but the service at buffet could have been better.

reviews.author: Pearl Chiu
reviews.text:
I want to see Moises next trip and the restaurant.
But not the resort

reviews.author: Saad S
reviews.text:
The hotel itself is really beautiful and the views inside and outside are amazing. I did not really have any issues with the hotel layout and cleanliness etc.
The main issue I had was the food and the shows. I did not feel that there was that great of quality food there besides maybe 1 restaurant which was at the Reserve. I think they need to step up on the food there and it will be great.
Second there were not that many shows or activities at the resort to do throughout the day. I think that they need to look at creating more fun activities for couples/families to experience.

reviews.author: Alexander Carpenter
reviews.text:
A really nice hotel with a good selection of restaurants and bars, the entertainment was really good and the kids club was exceptional.

The rooms did not match the hotel unfortunately and although the beds were comfortable they rooms were not set up correctly and falsely advertised.

We booked a junior suite with lagoon view for 5 people, 2a 3c, we arrived to find the room on the ground floor with no view atall as there was a wall in front of the terrace blocking any possible view of the lagoon.

The room only had a king-size bed in it, an unmade sofa bed and a separate room with 3 chairs in, no other beds. In my opinion, the hotel knew we were 5 and gave us a room with 1 bed, for a 5 star hotel this isn't acceptable, at the very least the sofa bed should have been made up.

After 2 days we were given another room which was on the third floor and had the view of the lagoon, this room was smaller so essentially a downgrade as it did not have the separate room and bathroom as the other one did, however we did manage to get 2 smaller beds instead of 1 bigger one and a cot for our youngest, in all honesty the lack of comfort really let the hotel down and unfortunately certain staff members made us feel like we shouldn't have an issue with the rooms given not being as advertised.

Additional incidents that let the hotel down we're when I cut my foot in the swimming pool on a piece of glass, I received medical treatment from the hotel to remove the glass, which I was very grateful of until I was presented with a waiver that I felt forced to sign saying that I refused medical treatment on site and that I exonerate the hotel from any wrong, this was wrong in my opinion.

reviews.author: Moon Chung
reviews.text: I was at this hotel with my son and my friend about 5years ago. I really had good memories and I brought my whole family. But this time I am not really satisfied how hotel has become. All the restaurants first come first serve. Begin serving at 6pm and everyone standing line since 5:30pm and got there at 9pm and said it's done because of waiting list.that is crazy. How can this hotel 5star with this system.  Before had to make reservation day before and be there at the time.and food wise it's got way worst then before. And hotel outside chair has broken and don't come to change. I would not recommend anymore. I have recommended to many of my friends past years but I guess no more...

reviews.author: JH K
reviews.text:
I want to first dispel this notion that adult guests must upgrade to The Reserve to enhance their all-inclusive experience. My wife and I didn't pay extra for it and we were glad that we didn't because all the space exclusive for The Reserve guests looked boring. The pool was eerily too quiet and the common areas was a complete ghost town.

Anyone who've ever stayed at other luxurious all-inclusive resorts in Cancún will know what I'm talking about when I say that the workers here are not overly friendly. From the beginning, I've noticed that the bell boys appeared continuously overwhelmed and weren't very good managing their stress. They started snapping at the guests because they were overwhelmed and the rudest one of them all is this older short gentleman with a buzz haircut. When we were leaving the resort, we were waiting at the bell desk to store our bags and there was a couple ahead of us.  He already didn't liked where we were standing so he told us to stand somewhere else. As he was helping the couple in front of us, he suddenly turned to us and told us in a very rude tone, "I'm not the only one working here. You can ask anyone who is dressed like me for help." Let me preface this by saying that we weren't staring at him, pressuring him, or even remotely accusing him of going too slowly. We were just talking to one another and not even facing this guy when he suddenly went into this tirade.  The workers at the check-in counter weren't rude but not overly nice either. I've also never been to a luxurious all-inclusive resort in Cancún where so many of the workers couldn't speak English.  For example, the lady working inside the van cooking meals by the pool couldn't even understand English. She was turning to the other employee to help her understand what I was requesting. The maintenance workers spoke very little English but more on them later in this review. Resort seems to cater more towards locals and other Spanish speakers.

Initially, we were very pleased with the room that we were assigned. We paid for the lagoon view but ended up getting a room with a partial ocean view. The room was spacious and had 2 full baths.  The problem with the room started when we came back from the pool to take a shower.  We had no hot water and we had to call the front desk to have maintenance come take a look. After a lot of wasted water and time, we finally got lukewarm water that was not suitable for showering. However, fixing one bathroom did not fix the other bathroom so we had to call for maintenance once again. We were able to get hot water coming out of the second bathroom so we had assumed the problem was somewhat resolved. The next day, we had the same exact problem. We called maintenance and had them fix the hot water problem again. One of the bathrooms just couldn't get hot water suitable for showering and the worker basically told us that that was the best that he could do.  For a resort that charged this much, this place was such a disappointment.

We did not eat at Sal Steak Cave, Cappella, or Santé.  Malva Food Bazaar is where breakfast is served and expect a long line. There are endless number of foods to eat; however, not much is very appetizing. There are two omelet stations manned by a female and a male employee. The female employee was extremely slow compared to the male employee. We liked Agua Marina (overall) and few dishes from Cielo. Lemon Fish was good but the rice that they used for the sushi was too damp and mushy (i.e. not sushi grade material). Many of the guests chose to avoid eating at Flora and I didn't blame them. Blue Agave has underwhelming food with extremely slow service. I saw a cockroach crawl past us at both Blue Agave and Malva (read other reviews about their cockroach problems).

With all that said, this resort is grand and beautiful. Loved the water flowing and live plants growing inside. I know there were a lot of negative things said in this review; however, we had fun nonetheless. Pools were also grand and views were spectacular. Would consider returning if changes were made.

reviews.author: Chris Jungclas
reviews.text:
Pros: Service was phenomenal. Staff was extremely friendly. Hotel was well maintained. The spa was expensive pricing $160 USD for 50 minute massage but one of the best massages I've gotten.

Cons: For a luxury all-inclusive resort the food was atrocious. Imagine a golden corral that is 2 days old. I think it's a supply chain problem and the quality of food they are getting is not good. We went during the hot season. This hotel is not prepared for it, the room never reached above 78F, the rest of the hotel is in the 80s and the pool water was like taking a bath. We were advised that there would be seaweed in advance and we're not surprised to find the beach unusable. See the attached picture for an example of a medium rare steak - disgusting. There was not a single restaurant that was up to our very low standards.

reviews.author: Annie Beyer-Chafets
reviews.text:
Highlights— beautiful hotel, got food poisoning, pushy staff will not help you unless you are constantly tipping.

They asked us many times if we were celebrating anything, and when we told them we were here for our honeymoon, they did not do anything special (I get if you don’t want to give us anything, but then why ask?) Our friends in the same building received complimentary champagne and fresh fruits when they arrived, and when we requested the same, we were told that we needed to give them more notice to order something special. When I told them our friends received this without asking, we were told that since we weren’t with our concierge “since day 1” he didn’t know if he should send us something. (Whatever that means?)

Service was highly inconsistent, some days we were being constantly flagged down by staff asking if we needed anything, looking for tips, and other days we would be ignored completely and would have to ask several times for basic things like water being stocked in our room. I have no problem going to the bar and and asking for my own drinks, but given that we were tipping and paid extra to stay in the reserve, I was a bit confused as to why we were not receiving the included services.

The spa has very limited facilities, no hot tub (none on site at all) and costs $30 per day to access just the sauna etc if you are not getting a treatment. You cannot use your melia spa vouchers for anything except a full priced 50 or 70 minute treatment.

The food is quite bad and hard to get unless you want to take your chances at the buffet — the restaurants do not take reservations and the wait times are over an hour for dinner. Restaurants keep hours and menus that are inconsistent with what’s on the app, so it’s hard to plan. The steakhouse, the only restaurant that takes reservations and costs extra, was the worst meal we had here — had to wait over an hour from the reservation time to even receive water, our order was wrong but the kitchen closed before we could even get our ordered sides, but by the end of it we just wanted to get out of there and eat snacks from the mini bar.

Our friends got sick from eating at Sante, the restaurant that is private to the reserve guests and always smells like sewage, and we suspect we either got food poisoning from Sante or Lemon Fish, the Japanese restaurant that others have said they’ve gotten food poisoning from (I stayed away from the raw fish and thought I’d be safe, oh well.)

When we tried to extend our room for one night to allow us to recover from the food poisoning, we were told by receptionist Violeta that it would be fine but that we had to wait for someone who was authorized to come back from making bracelets on the beach to finish the transaction. After waiting almost an hour and nearly throwing up in the lobby, I was told that our room was no longer available and that we had to move to a different room. I had really hoped that after spending thousands of dollars here and paying another $600 to postpone our trip home we could just get back into bed, but no. I was trying to be understanding about the fact that I got sick eating the food here, I did not blame anyone at the hotel or ask for anything free, but after the way I was treated the last thing I want to do is stay here another night and risk eating the food again. We also tried to see the hotel doctor, who costs $180 for a consultation but cannot provide medication or testing (what’s the point?) We paid out of pocket for a bunch of over the counter medications at the gift shop, packed up our room, moved to a new one, and finally got into bed. What a way to end our trip. No one seemed interested in helping us at any stage of this ordeal, and after a trip that was otherwise quite mediocre, I can’t imagine returning.

My husband didn’t want me to post this review while we are still staying here for fear of being mistreated as a consequence. But I’m posting now because I see that the hotel responds to these negative reviews by saying they wish they had gotten the feedback in real time. So I’m trying.

reviews.author: Aly K.
reviews.text: The hotel and beach were nice, but I didn't like the bathroom – the shower was weak, and there was no fan. The restaurant and food were okay, but not many options for vegetarians. Some workers were nice, but not all. Overall, the trip was okay. Would I go again? No. I've been to Cancun before and stayed at Hilton Cancun Mar Caribe All (used to be Royal Uno), and I really enjoyed it. The food, service, and room were amazing.

reviews.author: Kanika
reviews.text: The swimming pools have extremely cold freezing water. We took day pass at the neighboring hilton resort which and wonderful warm pool water with lots of pool activities.   Also there's no entertainment or music for teenagers and young adults at night.  We are here and disappointed.

reviews.author: Carine Pierre
reviews.text:
Pro: The property is very pretty. Plenty of spots to relax and take pictures. Valeria at the reserve pool provided excellent service and was very professional. Most of the staff are friendly
Cons: customer service is a joke. It feels like they’re constantly trying to squeeze money out of you even though they claim to be all-inclusive. Paying for upgrade was a waste of money. We upgraded to “the reserve” because we were told you’ll get access to premium services and drinks. But at the Italian restaurant, they only had one type of red and white wine, one has to pay extra for the others.  The meal options that seemed delicious and specials of the chef were at extra cost at that restaurant. The green bar juice didn’t have juice for all 3 nights & days we were there. The entertainment was just blah. The food was average (the fish at the Aquamarina has zero seasoning). The only food that tasted super delicious were offered at the Kanna and next to the adult only pool. We’ve been to several other resorts and this was by far the less customer service centered hotel we’ve been to. We read a lot of reviews and still wanted to give them a try. The reviews rating them average didn’t lie.

reviews.author: Vanessa C
reviews.text:
First and foremost, the staff gets 5 stars. They were absolutely amazing. I will provide you with names with places below.
Checking in: Upon your arrival, you walk into Tower three. I read that you are to be served a drink from when you walk in however, that was not provided. As noted, we paid extra for the reserved package. I was surprised that while regular guest were provided an air-conditioned lounge to check in, we were told to walk pass two towers to find the reserve check in area in the heat. Our room wasn’t ready, we had to wait an hour, so we sat with the concierge Abel. He told us that the reservations for the restaurants were no longer applicable and that they got rid of that three weeks ago. This is something I wish we would have known prior to us leaving to our vacation because nowhere on the website does it say this information. Throughout our stay, Abel did acknowledge my birthday by sending a treat to our room, and helped us with a reservation to their steakhouse. However, when it came to verify whether or not the Italian restaurant on site had any gluten-free options, it was like pulling teeth.  It took him a long time to respond to me to see whether or not I am able to eat at that restaurant, which by the time he had confirmed that they had a gluten-free options, it was too late to eat there.
Restaurants: If you have a gluten allergy, do not come here. The options for food are extremely low. I also am allergic to corn therefore, I hardly was able to eat much.
