Lemon fish: This place is Japanese infused and mainly serve sushi. The manager Daniel gave the absolute best service ever. Since this restaurant was in tower three, reserved area is in tower five, I was not able to consume the alcohol that they had there due to my allergies. Daniel was nice enough to have someone go to the reserved area and get the type of liquor that I could drink. Miguel was our server and he was the only server out of the whole weekend that started with a question “Do you have any food allergies?” I was very thankful that he cared to ask and was able to make my own sushi roll that did not contain gluten or corn. It was my birthday, so they brought me some fruit and sang happy birthday to me. Daniel and Miguel went above and beyond for my birthday and I really appreciate them for that.
Sal (steakhouse)- Not a lot of gluten-free options since a couple of their meats are marinated. While the restaurant was great, and the service was good, our server was Ignacio, I would not recommend their version of a top sirloin. I asked for medium, however it came out medium rare, and I was not able to cut into it. Our server did ask if I wanted another steak however, at that point I was over it.
Sante- We ate breakfast here every morning, this is strictly only for reserve guests. The views are beautiful and the food was decent.  Servers like Moises and Luis made our trip. I was having a tough time not being able to eat much and Moises was so funny and full of life that he made my day just with his laugh.
The Spa/Salon: I called the salon to see if they would be able to give me at least a blowout and if possible, curl my hair. I spoke to Alfredo, who informed me that the salon was going under renovations. However, he was going to call me back and see what he could do. Within minutes he called back and gave me the good news that they could take me in. When I got there, Christina and Isabell took care of me.  Isabell did such a great job on my hair and I am so grateful that they were able to take me in on my birthday.
Overall, would I ever come back? Absolutely not. While the staff was incredible, the food was mediocre. I appreciate that they acknowledged my birthday, and everyone would greet you every single morning, noon, and or night. The views and beach were beautiful. Did I feel like VIP? Not really. While having better liquor was great, I’m not much of a drinker, I expected better from the restaurants.

reviews.author: Joyce Vera
reviews.text:
Overall, it was a nice experience.
Pros: The service was incredible. Shout out to all the staff in the resort. They made our stay totally worth it. The beach was beautiful, and the seaweed wasn't an issue. Plenty of towels were available in the pool area. The staff were attentive constantly asking if we needed anything. Food and drinks were easily accessible. The pools were clean. The outside area of the resort was well maintained. We paid extra for the Reserve side (adults only), and we loved it. There were appointed cabanas, with appointed servers, and activities such as water acrobatics. It was calm and relaxing. I recommend it.
Inside the resort, it is beautiful with lots of plants and ponds. There are many sitting areas to relax and enjoy the views. There are two main bars inside the resort. The drinks were great. The bars outside close early, but there's a bar inside that stays open late. We saw a couple of shows. They were fun. Yoga sessions by the beach were available. Make sure to check the activities agenda. Housekeeping kept our room clean with fresh towels and stocked our bar fridge. Our air conditioner worked very well in the third room.
Cons: The reviews were right. The food is average, nothing special. A reservation is needed for most restaurants. My suggestion is to call ahead. The rooms need  an update. We had to change our room twice. In the first room, the tub got flooded when I showered. The water got up to my calf.  In the second room, there was no TV in the room, and the air conditioner wasn't working. Finally, we got a decent room in the 3rd level. The restrooms inside the resort were always dirty. The outside restrooms near the beach were way cleaner. Room service was terrible. It took more than an hour to get our food, and the food was awful.
Overall, excellent service. Mediocre rooms and food.

reviews.author: Mateo Felipe
reviews.text:
wanted to leave an actual review of paradisus cancun that wasn’t just supporting my beloved abraham, the bartender, at ginger bar so here we go! overall, im leaving this resort feeling very ambivalent with my experience.

beginning with the downsides:
- the pool bar bartenders were a bit passive and disregarding towards myself and my friend. they truly look lifeless as they poured me my 5th miami vice (which i can’t blame them for, but you gotta throw on a happy face when you come to work, i dont care).
- the overall layout of the hotel is confusing, and no, not because i was drinking, but because i swear everytime i walk down a hallway, i am transported into a new area ive never seen before, despite that being the same hallway.
- specifically at lemonfish, one of the restaurants here, we had the most frantic waiter who was just eager to get us out of the restaurant as soon as possible. he would take plates and drinks without permission, the drinks were terrible, and the food was mediocre. one of the weakest restaurants here despite its beautiful ambiance.
- the “no shoes no service” whatever rule that they have here is pretty misogynistic to be quite frank. why is it that old man joe can walk around with his honkers out, but my good sis josephine can’t wear a bathing suit top? double standards and unfortunately its not the 1800s, let women wear bikini tops.
- i am not sure what this resorts’ definition of “room service” is, but it is definitely not take an hour just to give me new towels and tuck in my sheets while leaving trash in the trash cans and no vaccuuming at all.
- the hours for restaurants and stores are very random and sometimes inconvenient. everything closes relatively early so there would be nights were we got ready to go to the bar, and we would have like an hour to enjoy ourselves. definitely a place to go to if you like to daydrink.

now for the upsides:
- most of the staff here are the most amicable & polite people ever, especially since we’re tourists and they literally owe us nothing. abraham at ginger bar making some amazing drinks, philoberto (sp?) introducing me to one of the best hamburgers ive ever had considering we’re in mexico, pablo at the concierge, carmen and tanya at yhi spa, and so on.
- the yhi spa is truly an experience, although pretty pricey, the massages me and my friend received along with the calming pool area was the highlight of this trip. truly refreshing and breathed new life into me after all the booze & heat.
- overall gorgeous architecture and truly almost every spot in this hotel is a wonderful photo opportunity
- phenomenally tasty food in practically every restaurant, even the buffet of all places! seasoned so perfectly, i am astounded. the drinks as well have been made very well!

overall, i had a very middle-of-the-road experience here at paradisus cancun. i don’t think i would return solely because i believe there are more resorts (i have visted two other resorts so far here in cancun) that will provide more services and joy for the same price, if not less. i wish there were an app of some sort that would provide hours, a digital map, & many other services that could easily streamline all the different amenities.

reviews.author: Jorge Perez
reviews.text:
Including this Hotel " Paradisus Cancun" I've been to other 3 paradisus properties and this one has been the worst yet. ill give this hotel 3 stars because its lacking a lot of what an all inclusive resort should be.
the Property its over 30 years old and you can see all over how its just falling apart. while they seem to be slowly sort of fixing some things the major places like the main pool needs some major renovation as well as the rooms. Never got to use the Balcony Jacuzzi because it did not look enticing at all, old and dirty seems to be the norm throughout. The food was ok at best. just like many places as soon as you walk in they start selling you extremely overpriced things left and right. and if you have resort credit just disregard it cuz it's worthless. Over all unfortunately I cannot recommend this hotel because with a few hundred more for the week im sure you can stay at a much much better and newer hotel. This place its just falling apart.

reviews.author: Sue Skaff
reviews.text: Beautiful resort, beautiful views.  Staff could of been more attentive, accommodating and pleasant.  The best waiters were in the breakfast buffet - they were exactly as what you would expect in a resort.  They were very happy, pleasant people.   Most of the sother staff were not concerned if we enjoyed our stay or not.  We did not feel we got what we paid for and will not stay there again.

reviews.author: Colleen Mcenaney
reviews.text: Karina and Abraham were amazing. All the pool staff was on point for the music festival. I was kind of dissapointed the alcohol was changed to bottom shelf though us older people can't drink that stuff.  Also The resident cat daisy is my favorite I hope she is well.

reviews.author: Natalie Maldonado
reviews.text:
In response to what management said on my email below, most intelligent adults do not put their legal name on google. Everything in my review was completely accurate and the staff was informed during my stay. There isn’t any response management can offer to change the experience. FACTS are FACTS.

*Definitely not for a couples getaway! There are a lot of children in every single corner of the resort. There is no adult-only anything and if there is then it definitely isn’t enforced. My husband and I literally had to leave the pool and other social areas that we were paying to enjoy just to avoid people’s kids.

Music blares all night and it’s not good music.

The buffet is the best food at the resort. Restaurants are a 2-3 on their best night. Very disappointing. I resorted to wings from room service every night to survive. I’m being dramatic, but I didn’t eat one complete meal from any restaurant that I thoroughly enjoyed.

The pillows have a terrible odor, like someone passing gas every time air is pushed out of it. Had our room changed because we thought the room was the issue, only to get to another room and discover the same exact odor, which we found was coming from the pillows.

Also, you get asked to take their “membership” or “timeshare” tour and they give you a gift certificate to the steakhouse. This certificate will probably pay for 1 drink. The steakhouse isn’t good and the wine I was given tasted old and cheap but they charge top dollar for it. I took 1 bite of my steak and potato and threw the rest away but still had to pay the $150 bill.  I suggest going out to eat at a nice restaurant instead of spending money here.

Customer service is good, they try their best.

This resort is a solid 3 stars due to customer service. Based on my experience, I will not return here.

reviews.author: Wade Ha
reviews.text:
It was a truly satisfying trip.

I would like to leave a few comments in the hope that Paradisus Cancun will become an even more famous and wonderful resort. I visited this place with a friend and stayed for four days.

Having traveled to Cancun about five times, I have stayed at everything from mid-range to the most expensive luxury resorts. Based on this experience, I compared Paradisus Cancun to other places.

1. System

Perhaps because the resort recently reopened, its systems are significantly lacking compared to other resorts. I stayed here on a weekday, and the experience of having to search for a restaurant that was fully booked because I could not make a reservation for dinner was not pleasant.

In particular, the fact that meal reservations and event attendance bookings cannot be made via the smartphone application was very inconvenient compared to other resorts. It was truly unpleasant to have to wait for over an hour at the concierge from the morning just to make a reservation for dinner.

2. Information

It was difficult to read the map, whether in the application or the catalog. I had to search for quite a while because I didn't know where or on which floor the restaurant was located, and it was difficult to find out when and where various events were being held. The information provided by the smartphone application was complex and difficult to view at a glance.

3. Food/Dessert

The quality of the food and desserts was excellent. The ingredients were fresh, and it did not feel like cheap ingredients were being used. You can usually tell immediately if cheap ingredients are being used for desserts, but these were incredibly delicious.

Room service was also very neat and delicious, so I was satisfied.

4. Staff

All the staff worked incredibly hard, to the point where they looked exhausted.

In particular:

Front Desk - Roberto: He was very responsible and instilled confidence.

KAO Bar - Salvador: He was friendly and brought joy to those waiting.

It was pitiful to see the staff responding kindly even when guests who couldn't get dinner reservations were making strong complaints (even though this wasn't the fault of either the guests or the staff).

5. Overall Review

Like me, people visit Paradisus Cancun to spend a lot of money on a vacation. While everyone has different expectations, I believe Paradisus Cancun pursues one single direction: customer satisfaction.

To become a resort that everyone wants to visit, improvements are needed in the areas that are currently problematic. I believe that with just a little more development, it could become the best resort.

The staff are truly doing their best, but it was disappointing that the resort's internal systems did not seem to be functioning 100%.

I don't usually write reviews like this, but I am leaving this one because I believe it could become perfect with just a few changes. If I have the opportunity to visit again, I hope the issues I pointed out have been improved to surprise me. I especially hope the resort continues to improve, for the sake of all the staff members who were so kind to me.

reviews.author: MÓNICA MORÁN
reviews.text:
The hotel is very nice, but it needs some cleaning and maintenance. The restaurant entrance process is very slow. Sometimes you have to wait in lines for 15 minutes. Although food is always available, you have to wait up to an hour to get into the only restaurant open from 4 to 6 p.m. Room service has a charge just to have it delivered, which I find inappropriate.
The service is divided: you either get someone who serves you very well or you get very bad service.
There aren't enough lounge chairs.

reviews.author: Imanol Santano
reviews.text: It's a great hotel, but there's a clear, huge difference between the services it offers, like restaurants and pools, and the rooms. The former are renovated and new, while the latter are completely neglected and poorly maintained. They advertise it as a junior suite, but it's just a regular hotel room; it's not a suite at all. The reception staff is unfriendly and doesn't make you feel like you're in a four-diamond hotel. We had a major problem, and it was guest services who helped us, not reception. Overall, given the wide range of quality hotels nearby, this one isn't worth it.

reviews.author: Pri Sommelier
reviews.text: What can I say about Paradisus (extra charge for The Reserve category)? We arrived on Sunday and left Saturday morning. Even on Sunday, when we arrived, the receptionists didn't know where to send us to eat. We had to rely on our own intuition to find somewhere to eat, since beach bars and restaurants close at 4 pm. We managed to get cold cuts and cheeses at the cafeteria. It's worth noting that we weren't offered any drinks or anything at reception. Monday morning wasn't any better. For breakfast at Sante, we ordered scrambled eggs, which arrived without bread because they were out. They didn't know how to fix it. Two days later, at another breakfast, the bread arrived, and 50 minutes later, the eggs (very disappointing). The sun loungers without shade at the pools or beach designated for The Reserve guests (not exclusive at all) were available. We learned from the assigned concierge that you only have two days during your entire stay to use the shaded loungers (again, very exclusive). It's worth mentioning that alcohol stops at 11 PM throughout the hotel, and the minibar only has beer. If you order wine, it's the same for the entire hotel, costs $9, and you won't have access to it in your room. The hotel is geared towards Americans; they always speak to you in English and provide better service if you speak English. None of the service staff seem to know the hotel's operating hours. Please don't use room service; it takes an hour and a half to get a burger and wings, and when you ask for ice, it never arrives. The restaurants are decent. Capella is bad (overcooked pasta and sour sauce), Agua Marina is okay (they take your food away before you finish, which makes it bad), Sante is decent for dinner, Sal is good if you like American-style meat (charred on the outside but cooked to perfection), Malva is acceptable for a buffet and has some highlights, although it's always packed. Mascalzone is decent for stone-baked pizza (they don't have calzones or mushrooms). The lemon fish sushi was forgettable, but the octopus was outstanding. The Flora was delicious, with good use of ingredients and friendly service. I especially appreciated the service from the gentleman at the Nespresso café in The Reserve area! In short, a beautifully decorated hotel with sublime architecture, terribly managed and forgettable for the price.

reviews.author: lorena lodeiro
reviews.text:
Good evening, I'm staying at the hotel right now, today is my first day.
I agree with Sebastián's opinion (below). I don't understand why an "all-inclusive" hotel doesn't offer "everything included." What do I mean by that? I've stayed at other hotel chains where I didn't have to pay extra for meat. I can't believe that I have to pay extra to go to two of their restaurants. I've never experienced this before. The same goes for the wines; only two are included, and they aren't the best.
The signage isn't good; finding the Flora restaurant was difficult. However, I can't say anything negative about the service; Cinthia and Fanny were excellent, and the food was exquisite. We booked the highest Meliá category, Paradisus, so I didn't expect these things to be excluded. The same goes for the sun loungers (I don't remember what they're called here); they cost extra, unlike the regular lounge chairs, which are included. It's a real shame, I didn't expect it to be like this.
The room we got was perfect, comfortable, and cool (thankfully). The Flora restaurant is hot. All areas close at 11 pm; if you want something to eat or drink after that time, it's room service. And depending on your room category, they might deliver two or three times.
The only thing open 24 hours is the coffee area, where they serve something sweet or a savory sandwich.

reviews.author: Hector Lozano
reviews.text:
We have been coming to this hotel for many years. Lately, we have noticed a difference in the quality of service. There are not enough staff to meet the demand from guests. Going to a hotel restaurant means having to wait a long time to be attended to, served, etc. In the pool area, there are not enough servers. Food is constantly running out at the basic stations around the pool. The Malva restaurant (buffet) has declined in food quality. There are long lines to be seated.
We are very disappointed with how the quality of service has declined at what used to be a great hotel.

reviews.author: César
reviews.text: "I DO NOT RECOMMEND THAT HOTEL." I stayed from March 28th to 31st, 2025, and my reservation, paid a month in advance, was for a Junior Suite with an OCEAN VIEW. Upon arrival, I was assigned a room on the ground floor with a view of a nearly two-meter-tall planter, with a patio (it can't really be called a balcony) with exposed plumbing and no chairs or table. When I complained to the staff, they told me that the hotel has that floor and those rooms listed as having an ocean view, that the planters are for hurricane protection, and that they were currently fully booked. They said they could move me to another floor the following day, provided there was availability. When I requested a full refund of my reservation or a proportional refund for the room, they refused, arguing that since it was booked through an agency, I had to complain to them. The facilities are very nice, as are the beach and pools; the bar staff and some waiters are not rude but not friendly either.

reviews.author: YOLY AM
reviews.text:
My expectations were high, and to my taste, it left much to be desired. I think they have a lot of room for improvement in terms of value for money. The only redeeming feature of my stay was the Aguamarina restaurant; the service was excellent, especially from Renan, who was very attentive, helpful, friendly, and fun.

Thank you, Renan, for your attention and good humor.

reviews.author: Elenice Teixeira
reviews.text:
Excellent work by the recreation staff, special mention to Uriel's attentiveness and friendliness. Friendly with everyone, adults and children.
My reservation regarding the hotel services is that we paid for all-inclusive, but there are exceptions for everything: drinks, chairs on the beach and by the pool. The waiters only pay attention if you tip them; otherwise, they won't even come near you.

reviews.author: Rodrigo Rotenberg
reviews.text:
Disappointing Resort Experience – Distorted Priorities

Today, Thursday, September 26th, I'm in a cabana by the pool, right in front of the Água Marina restaurant. It's 10 am, the sun is strong, but the cabana should protect us and guarantee a moment of comfort and rest.

However, to my surprise, a hotel employee just removed the side curtains of the cabana, claiming they needed washing. The result? We were completely exposed to the sun. Is it really necessary to do this kind of maintenance in the middle of the morning, when guests are using the space?

It seems that, for the hotel, keeping a curtain shining is more important than preserving the comfort and experience of its customers. It's frustrating to realize that operational convenience has been prioritized over the needs of those paying for a relaxing and enjoyable experience.

Small details like this make all the difference in the guest experience and deserve to be reconsidered to improve the quality of service.

reviews.author: Biani Salas Morales
reviews.text: The Lemon Fish restaurant was the best of all; my waiters, Jorge and Arce (on two different days), gave me five-star service. The hotel staff in general are very friendly and make you feel at home. It's a shame that the hotel facilities are so run down and that there are leaks everywhere. The rooms have furniture from the 80s, and the bathrooms are practically unusable.

reviews.author: Valerie canuel
reviews.text:
We're currently staying at the Paradisus Cancun. It's an old but clean hotel. The service is very good.
It's difficult to get chairs on the beach if you don't book early in the morning. Our room was never cleaned by the housekeeper all week. The shower leaks under the sink; the room is nothing like a 5-star hotel. We found a cockroach in the room. The food is good, and the staff are generally very friendly. But I can't compare it to the other Paradisus hotels we've stayed at.

reviews.author: Daniel Serrano
reviews.text: Jesús Canche from the Capela restaurant was very attentive and always made sure our visit was pleasant. His service was excellent, but the food left much to be desired; it was a big disappointment.

reviews.author: Rocio Sanchez
reviews.text: It seems I got off on the wrong foot. I didn't feel as well taken care of as I have in other 5-star hotels I've stayed in. The facilities are very nice, but the staff service isn't very good. At the buffet, they don't even come near you to offer a glass of water, and don't even think about taking your food to your room, even if you have small children, because it's not allowed. I find it absurd. Also, not all the bars are open, including the lobby bar, which is one of the most important bars in a hotel. You have to reserve the daily specials, and you can't always find a spot. I really haven't felt comfortable.

reviews.author: Denisse Salazar
reviews.text: The location is super good, close to the shopping malls, aquarium etc. The atmosphere is a bit neglected, there are no signs so I got lost every day of my stay, the rooms are unclean, they don't sweep them, they only change the towels, so if you have sand on your clothes make sure you shake it off outside your room, the buffet food is the same, I didn't eat there the last 2 days because the taste had me sick, there was nothing that caught my attention, the dinner on the beach at the event was delicious, a steak with cream cheese risotto, I loved it!

reviews.author: Eloísa Cruz Rivas
reviews.text: The hotel service is very good overall, including room service, but especially the Malva Restaurant area, where the buffet offers a wide variety of foods for a light breakfast with cereal, fruit, salads, and much more! Excellent service from the young Enrique García, who is always attentive to all diners, whether foreign or Mexican. The service at the reservation restaurants is equally superb! I highly recommend eating at the Salt Restaurant! They have very special cuts of meat, excellent service with minimal wait times, and the restaurant itself is lovely!

reviews.author: Giselle Martínez
reviews.text:
I'll start by acknowledging the positive aspects of Paradisus.

The hotel's architecture is STUNNING, absolutely nothing bad to say about it. Every corner is spectacular.

The same goes for the staff and their service—a warm, family-like atmosphere, like being at home. If you see a staff member walking down the hallway, they'll ask about your day and how it's going. At the Malva restaurant, we received excellent service, especially from Mr. Alberto, and we were very grateful and happy thanks to him. We also received exceptional service at the coffee shop from a young man who, please excuse us for not knowing his name, but during our pleasant conversation, we forgot about that small detail. That, at least for us, is a huge plus. As for the kindness area, the staff were incredibly attentive, friendly, helpful, and fun. A big thank you to Irlanda, Gove, Azul, Nani, Monse, and Yami 🫶🏻

As for the negative aspects, which are of utmost importance to us, we left quite disappointed; It's their food.
Most of the time we ate at Malva.
The low quality and lack of care and hygiene are noticeable. It's always cold (except for the soups and creams), tastes bad, or is often from previous days. At Blue Agave, we literally ordered four tacos and it took 30 minutes to serve them.
We were there on a day of emergency due to Hurricane Berly, and for safety reasons, the convention area was set up for food consumption. That's where we confirmed the poor hygiene, as small cockroaches were crawling on the bread boxes (bread that's always exposed to the open air). Again, I have nothing bad to say about the service and attention from the staff, but the food left much to be desired. We had stomach problems every day and had to go out to find somewhere to eat. This, along with the fact that it's very hot and humid inside the hotel, makes us want to look for other options for our next visit.

reviews.author: Carolina Dosdoglirian
reviews.text:
We stayed at the hotel for a few days!
It's very nice, but I had been there a few years ago and the quality has gone down considerably. We weren't completely convinced.

I want to highlight Jorge's service at the Lima Fish restaurant; we had an amazing meal and he gave us great advice.

Also, Laura's beach service was fantastic—she was wonderful, bringing us food and being incredibly friendly.

Management should modernize or hire more staff; there are queues for breakfast and coffee, and the Italian restaurant is a rather unattractive section of the buffet.

reviews.author: Emiliano Ariel Torcal
reviews.text: My partner and I stayed here less than a month ago. The staff was very friendly, but the service left something to be desired. The information they provided was either scarce or incorrect; we had several instances where the staff told us one thing and then said another. The room was nice but had several flaws. The air conditioning was very noisy, the light switches had strange combinations, there were only four outlets in the entire room—two in the bathroom (which didn't work) and two on the sofa, none near the bed, and the curtain rods weren't attached to the curtains and were useless. Overall, a mediocre experience, with some good points and some not so good.

reviews.author: Sam
reviews.text:
It was a pleasant experience, but there were a lot of things I had to complain about, and I complained to guest service.

First of all, my flight arrived at 8:00 AM and I got to the hotel almost at 9:00 AM. The kids had their baths and everything, but the water wouldn't drain. The toilet was clogged, and we called someone to fix it. It took an hour, and they wouldn't give us another room until the next day. The internet was down for almost a day; the door was broken, and we couldn't get in. I had to wait until noon for them to change the battery outside the room, with the kids already asleep. The drinks are served in plastic cups—awful! Imagine seeing a margarita presented like that. Also, if you didn't get to the beach early to grab a chair or something to sit on, you had to stand or sit on the sand. On the last day, I went to the hotel's taco stand, and the waiter saw us when we raised our hands, but they didn't serve us. The glasses we requested were missing, and the waiter noticed but never provided them. Our chips and guacamole arrived 20 minutes later, while the next table that arrived after us was served much faster. The waiter was giving us strange looks. Room service was completely unhelpful and refused to apologize; we had to call the manager.

I don't recommend this place if you're staying in Cancun.

reviews.author: Cristian Vargas Avilés
reviews.text:
The hotel is very well renovated, quite pleasing to the eye, and when you arrive, you get the impression that it's a super luxurious hotel and that the service is going to be incredible, BUT, the truth is, it's not.
The rooms are quite rustic. The shower water spills out because the curtain is too short. There's also no non-slip mat. There's no notebook or pen for notes. The furniture is old, and the drawers are falling apart.
The service at the pool is quite poor. There are almost no waiters, and those who are there are reluctant to approach. The bartenders are rude and seem bothered by making drinks.
There aren't enough umbrellas, much less lounge chairs; everything is occupied by 8 a.m. They have plenty of Balinese beds, which cost exorbitantly $250 a day.

reviews.author: Gisele Naves
reviews.text: When we chose this "luxurious" hotel, it was initially because we thought it would be a good place to go with the family; we have a 2-year-old and 7-month-old daughter, and she is our priority. The cost-benefit ratio it offered seemed attractive. There were three of us: me, my husband, and our daughter. But right from the start, at reception for check-in, the reception area was crowded and very hot, and the people there, except for the baggage handlers, weren't very friendly and seemed quite eager to "get rid of us." Anyway, some things about the hotel were explained to us since we booked the "all-inclusive" package. When we went to the room, the first unpleasant thing was that I was surprised by someone who was going to clean the room. We had just arrived, we were taking a shower, and he simply opened the door to clean a room that was theoretically already clean. It wasn't his mistake, of course, but the hotel's, since the room was reserved for that day and time. Also, the room we booked had a view of the lagoon, but in reality, it only had a view of one end of the lagoon, haha. When we went to the pool, the only time we received prompt and good service was when we sat facing the sea at one of the overpriced kiosks they try to rent you. Around the pool there are few kiosks and "free" spaces, so why do they try to sell you these overpriced ones? It's ridiculous. Oh, and those places were always empty. The waitresses had a sour face and were unwilling to help from beginning to end, except for one named Hugo who was always kind. Of course, the service is very different when you offer a tip, but you hotel managers and employees can't forget that kindness and politeness are not a differentiator, but an obligation. They try to sell you everything there, and they are insistent. The restaurants, even when empty, require reservations, except for two that were very crowded and had queues, but they are better than some of the others. I was pleasantly surprised by the Enzo restaurant, which serves Asian food, and especially by the waiter José. The best in my opinion. The noise at night is excessive and continues all night. I made a complaint about the noise, but it didn't help at all. And to top it all off, on the last day the maid didn't provide face towels; something was missing every day. But here's a tip: Cancun is wonderful and worth visiting, I just don't recommend this hotel. I don't recommend it because for what it offers (treatment, politeness, respect, food, all-inclusive which doesn't seem all-inclusive to me) it's not worth it. Oh, and there's a sign saying you can only use the pool until 8 pm, which I think is unnecessary, especially since there was loud music playing until late at night.

reviews.author: Lucia Mendizabal
reviews.text:
3-Star Hotel
I spent a week at Paradisus Cancun, and while it was a pleasant stay, I expected much more.
Positive points: The food quality is very good, the Nespresso bar, the beach, and the service from the bar staff and Uriel!
Negative points:
1- Any drink or cocktail is served in PLASTIC cups. A hotel of this category shouldn't serve a margarita or a tequila shot in a plastic cup... Furthermore, the drinks are of poor quality, mostly domestic brands, and some are even homemade and kept in jugs.

2- An exaggeratedly tipping-dependent culture. They even "indirectly" asked for tips, and if you don't give them one, the treatment changes drastically and becomes very unfriendly.

3- Don't go with children. We went with 13-year-olds who weren't even allowed in many of the hotel's public areas, even though they were with their parents. It was a family trip, and because of this, we had to stay separated or go straight back to our room since they weren't allowed in.

4- The rooms were nice, but we had problems with the bathroom (which, despite complaining, was repaired several days later), and the minibar wasn't restocked every day, only every other day if we were lucky.

As constructive criticism, I'd like to add that it's a shame you can't make reservations for dinner at the restaurants. We were with a large group, and it would have been much more convenient (for them and for us) to have been able to reserve a table for everyone together in advance for each dinner.

reviews.author: Ralu Chavez
reviews.text:
I honestly don't know what to say exactly. I had very high expectations, but once we got here, everything changed.
The only good thing was the doctor, who helped us a lot when our son got sick.
The restaurant staff, if you don't give them tips, they won't even bother you. The food is far inferior to all the hotels we've been to before. You can barely find anything to eat at the buffet. We liked the food at La Capella and Agua Marina, as well as the pizza next to the pool. We also liked the tacos al pastor and the tequila at Blue Agave.
The jacuzzi on the terrace of our room didn't work, but at least we used it as a mini-pool for our son.
They say it's a family hotel, but they don't have slides or things for children in the pool. Also, tonight I went with my son to see the children's show, and at the end, the lady shared candy with the kids, but when she got to mine, the candy was gone, and my son was sad. The lady didn't even apologize and didn't come back to get him anything. Anyway!
Not to mention the negatives, I liked the cleanliness and the fact that they always brought us water for the mini-fridge in the room.
If we're ever going back to Cancun, it definitely won't be at this hotel!

reviews.author: Catalina Nicole Amoruso Ribera
reviews.text: The staff got angry if you didn't tip them. The electricity was quite unreliable, and the power went out once. The hotel itself was very nice, and I had no other problems. A very good vacation! 🥳

reviews.author: Edgar Israel Gutierrez Palomares
reviews.text:
This is my second time at this hotel. The first time was great; I was given a remodeled room and the service was excellent. But two years later, when I returned, it was the complete opposite. I was assigned an old room with outdated furniture and a bathroom.

On the other hand, the reception staff's service leaves much to be desired. They have a terrible attitude; from the moment you arrive, they greet you rudely, are arrogant, and don't even look you in the eye. They're not very communicative, and I got the impression they don't like receiving domestic tourists. Honestly, with that attitude, I have no desire to return to this hotel.

The good things I will acknowledge are: the food is very good, both at the buffet and in the specialty restaurants; the waiters are very attentive and always ready to provide good service. I especially want to commend Atilano, Martín, Fernando, and Orlando. The hotel beach is nice, with plenty of lounge chairs and umbrellas; the bars in the pool area are good, and there are waiters on the beach.

reviews.author: Natalia Erazo Ruiz
reviews.text:
The hotel is very nice; the pools, restaurants, beach, and staff are excellent.

I have to mention a few things:
1. Upon check-in, we were given a room with two double beds facing a large, dark wall, even though we had reserved a king-size bed with a lake view. We told the receptionist that this wasn't our reservation, and she replied that even if we booked the room type we paid for, it wouldn't be the one we received. We made this reservation two months in advance.

2. The room cleaning service was disappointing. On two occasions, they didn't clean the room (it wasn't so much about cleaning, but about providing fresh towels and clean sheets). I had to call to have them come, something that had never happened to me before, and I've been to Cancun several times on all-inclusive trips.

3. Room service includes food, but you have to pay between $5 and $6 after the third order delivered to your room, so it's not fully included, and you have to call to have the dishes picked up, but sometimes they didn't come.

reviews.author: Marcela Pantoja
reviews.text: Good location, nice beach, but they need to significantly improve the quality and flavor of their food and drinks. Plus, you pay for an all-inclusive package, and when you use the facilities, you realize it's not all-inclusive and you have to pay extra to use certain areas, certain services, and even certain lounge chairs. There was a long line to get into the buffet; we didn't even get a seat at one of the included restaurants. Having a membership here doesn't guarantee you any benefits. I think it ends up being more expensive, and you realize it's expensive compared to the service you receive.

reviews.author: Luis Alberto Martínez
reviews.text:
The reception staff lacks much training.

They don't remove the sargassum from the beach. It's very annoying to swim in it...

The waiters in the restaurants are very attentive and friendly... the ones at the pool... there are very few and they take a long time to bring drinks...

The quality of the restaurants has dropped; the only notable thing is the Sante restaurant, which offers VIP service. And the SAL restaurant.

The buffet food is very bland, and the chilaquiles are very sour... the eggs are unsalted...

It's only worth staying at this hotel with a room in the Reserve or Nikté category.

reviews.author: Andrés Wehrle
reviews.text: Unfortunately, I didn't receive the level of service I'm used to from Meliá hotels. The food selection was very limited, and at breakfast, it took a long time to replenish the bread, cheese, fruit, and other items. What saved my stay were the spectacular service from Ramiro at the Malva Restaurant and from Cristian, Karina, and Gladys at the Ginger sports bar. On the negative side, I must highlight the very poor service and treatment I received from Ian at the Ginger bar.

reviews.author: Selma Alva
reviews.text: The service offered is completely uncompensated for the price. Waiters are either inattentive or rude, the minibar isn't restocked, and there's a clear bias towards foreign products. The food is nothing special and sometimes lacks flavor. The hotel is old and would appreciate some improvements, such as electrical outlets in the rooms or better door locks. The only good things were the decently equipped gym and the use of wristbands as room keys.

reviews.author: Graciela Gomez
reviews.text: If you're traveling in a group and don't plan on leaving the hotel, it's a good option. If your plan is to relax and enjoy personalized service, go somewhere else. This hotel caters to large crowds, with lots of people around, pool activities, children having fun, and large families. It's not worth going out since it's all-inclusive, so if you want to explore, look for a breakfast-only hotel. The service is good. The room is somewhat outdated, and only one of the cell phone charging outlets worked.

reviews.author: Claudia Bernal
reviews.text:
Unfortunately, our room had a clogged shower and cockroaches.
The rest of the facilities are good, with a nice view and several pools. The sea was very choppy, so we preferred to stay in the pool. The waiters' service was good. Breakfast didn't offer much variety; they had more sweet than savory options.

reviews.author: Poliana Coelho
reviews.text:
We've already been to another one of the same line, in Punta Cana, and it was flawless.
This one in Cancun, being a 5-star hotel, leaves much to be desired. From bathroom problems in the rooms to an elevator that fell with people inside!
The food wasn't great either. Plus, they were constantly standing in front of the pools offering excursions.

But the pools are great and the staff are very friendly.

reviews.author: ivan gonzalez
reviews.text:
The rooms are generally okay, but they feel outdated. There was a leak in the toilet that they supposedly fixed, but it kept happening. They no longer provide shampoo and bar soap, and they don't offer the complimentary goodnight greetings. The organization is poor, or there's bad communication, because when I arrived at the first room they gave me, they were painting it, and they gave me another one that hadn't been cleaned yet.
The buffet was mostly vegetables (about 80%), and the stews they had were very salty.
The service from some of the waiters was very, very bad; they had a terrible attitude. The pool had bits of trash floating in it—not a lot, but there were papers, leaves, and other debris. Oh, and please be careful with those who offer you a complimentary family photo, because in the end, the package they put together costs 9,000 pesos, and if you don't buy it, they get very rude. It's worth mentioning that the photos are very nice, but that's not the way to sell.

reviews.author: Fernando Mattera
reviews.text:
For the price of a single room (around $375 USD), the hotel could offer more and better services.

First of all, the buffet restaurant serves the exact same meals every day, and I'd give it a 6 out of 10, when it should be at least 8 or 9.
The waiters serve you listlessly and always with the clear objective of getting a tip, whether it's for breakfast, lunch, dinner, or even just a drink. A clear example was that I stayed for 10 days, and every time I ordered juice in a specific glass for breakfast, they gave it to me in a much smaller one, even though I clearly specified the size. Inside, I was thinking, "Don't worry, I'll tip you anyway," but no. Furthermore, when they realize from your tone of voice that you're Argentinian, they treat you with a peculiar contempt: they hate you, but they can't say it outright. If that hatred stems from the fact that they can never beat us at the national team level in the World Cup, work on that. It's not our fault. In fact, for us, Mexico is just another rival, but the hatred in the air is more than evident… guys, I went because the company invited me. Honestly, if you want me to pay out of my own pocket, get your act together.
The only good thing is the artificial paradise that is Cancún. Goodbye forever.

reviews.author: Tony Ng
reviews.text:
My wife and I decided to stay at the Paradisus Cancun because of an attractive offer, but our experience revealed some issues to consider. Although the architecture reflects luxury, we discovered aesthetic problems, such as damaged walls, mold, and areas in urgent need of renovation.

Service varied among employees, lacking consistency and showing signs of overwork. We would like to highlight Rosana from customer service, who resolved a crucial issue. However, other interactions were less satisfactory, including a negative experience with a customer service representative.

The quality of the food in the restaurants did not match the aesthetics. The lack of flavor and preparation of the dishes contrasted sharply with the visual presentation. Furthermore, the process of getting a table was inconvenient, with no reservation system and long waits.

The pool showed signs of neglect, and the daily struggle for beach chairs highlighted the hotel's lack of control over this problem. Service, while acceptable at the pool, was slow on the beach, where a single waiter was insufficient to cover the entire area.

In summary, the Paradisus Cancun, despite its potential, needs substantial improvements to meet the expectations of a five-star hotel. We recommend an immediate renovation, better staff training, implementation of a reservation system, addressing the issue of beach chairs, and increasing beach staff. The decision to return will depend on future improvements and competitive pricing.

reviews.author: luis pedraza
reviews.text: I went to a conference and the hotel had poor communication with the travel agency. I was overcharged, and the manager never showed up even though I requested him. The person who checked me in and made me pay extra never contacted me again to explain the problem. In the end, I managed to get a refund through the agency. We had to tip at the entrance of each restaurant to receive good service. Although it's all-inclusive, I recommend bringing cash to incentivize the staff, especially in restaurants. We tried to book a parasail, but there was no communication between the hotel and the provider, so we didn't go. The food was good, the beach was very nice, the pool was good, the drinks were good, we saw some very expensive off-menu items, the view was spectacular, the rooms were comfortable, but the bathroom was dark and old. I suggest setting aside money for extras and tipping before receiving service. The price was reasonable.

reviews.author: Agustin Carbo
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful and the beach is dreamy. The water is crystal clear. However, the hotel facilities and staff are inadequate for the number of guests. For example, if you go down after 9:30 am, you probably won't find a lounge chair on the beach or by the pool. I find this unacceptable. We spent two days with towels on the floor.

reviews.author: Vitor Gambassi
reviews.text: The hotel is quite impressive, with enormous ceilings and decor and structure reminiscent of cenotes. Everything is well-maintained, and the room is spacious and always very clean. The hotel is very close to the beach, as are the pool and some restaurants, making life much easier for those who are there to relax. The drinks are almost all top-notch, very good, and with very well-made cocktails. However, the food is quite weak. In every restaurant we ate at, something always went wrong, whether it was the food taking too long to arrive, being cold, or even bad (sometimes all of these things happened at once). The food was the hotel's weak point, a very weak point. One of the restaurants was under renovation, so they divided the breakfast and buffet among other, much weaker restaurants. On the last day, the restaurant opened, and we noticed the absurd difference it made, as it was truly much better than the others. This restaurant renovation was a rip-off, without any benefit to the customer who stayed there during that time. I do not recommend it because of this. We also had problems with the travel agency located in the hotel, OTIUM; we do not recommend them and ended up with a loss of $60. The hotel should look into this.

reviews.author: César Escobar B.
reviews.text:
It's very interesting to consider the following:
Nature has provided the entire hotel zone with a delicious and spectacular beach, so I can't consider it as a positive point in my evaluation.
However, I will consider its infrastructure, staff, food, and services.

Regarding infrastructure, I can mention that it's a large resort, worthy of admiration. Elegant, clean, and well-designed. I understand that managing such a large hotel requires time, dedication, and, above all, a lot of maintenance. The latter should be considered part of a comprehensive maintenance plan.
I give it 4 stars.

The staff are the best thing about the hotel, always very hospitable and with that warmth that Latinos are accustomed to. The entire staff always strives to make you feel comfortable.
I give it 5 stars.

Food. I still have the general feeling that the quality of the food wasn't the most satisfactory. In fact, I would say it's below average, regardless of the venues; whether around the pools or inside the hotel. Listing each location would be very painful. But overall, the cost-benefit ratio was a disappointment. Five consecutive days with the same dismay... That's a problem, and they should resolve it immediately. I don't consider myself a gourmet, but I do have a culinary culture, so I don't understand why they sacrifice their excellent staff to face their disgruntled customers? They're indirectly doing a disservice.
I'm giving it 1 star.

Service. The hotel's general services seem to me to be within standard, providing fun and entertainment.
I'm giving it 3 stars.

In short, the hotel's best feature is its staff. Staff that you should value, because they are the face of all the services they provide. But you have to admit, if something starts badly, everything ends badly.

Now ask yourself... would I recommend anyone come to this hotel?????

I really hope they make a change.

Finally, thanks to all the workers who made us feel better during my stay.

reviews.author: Cristian Zalles
reviews.text: The beach is very good, clean, and the sea is quiet, so you can swim. Perfect for kids. The rooms are old in the main tower. The air conditioning failed twice, so we had to change rooms, and the second one had the same problem. The buffet food wasn't bad, but it wasn't anything special either. At checkout, some people indicated that you could still use the facilities, while others indicated that you couldn't; they were poorly organized.

reviews.author: Jullissa Ng Chinkee
reviews.text:
Ivonn and Javier's service at Malva Cenas restaurant was fantastic.
Regarding the food, I would suggest a warmer temperature for the items that deserve it.

reviews.author: Luz Hernandez
reviews.text:
Very nice, but with some inconveniences...
The service was very poor...👉Except for Alejandro from Nespresso, who is a sweetheart and always in a good mood, and Michele from the buffet, who always has a smile.
The rest were very rude and unwilling to attend to customer requests beyond the basics...👎
We opted to go get our drinks ourselves to avoid responses like, "Order your drinks when everyone is here, otherwise I have to come back several times and do twice the work..."👎🤦🏼‍♀️🤷🏼‍♀️
Another staff member rudely reprimanded us because we changed tables since the one they had given us was in direct sunlight.🥴👎
This is unacceptable in a 5-star hotel where customer comfort should be the priority.

reviews.author: Maria Carla Martinez Caro
reviews.text:
Paradisus Cancun is a pleasant and aesthetically stunning all-inclusive.
My overall stay was good.
We had a great time and enjoyed some lovely family time.
The staff is good, except for the wait staff at the Malva and Capella restaurants.
Raul, our concierge, is a genius; he was very helpful, friendly, and fun!

reviews.author: Wendy Reyes
reviews.text: Overall, it's good. The hotel is very nice and has a wide range of staff, from excellent to terrible. The food quality is good. There are two negative points to highlight: they make a big distinction between domestic and international tourists, and they offer you membership in their "circle" club where they basically harass you and try to force you to buy things.

reviews.author: Ian Sampayo
reviews.text: The decoration is good and everything is nice but between 8 am and 12 pm you can't consume much since only one restaurant is open and the others are not and the same thing happens in the afternoons there is only one restaurant open and the others are closed.

reviews.author: Guillermo PS
reviews.text: I can recommend it, but I wouldn't return. The extra activities are very varied, the service on the beach is slow, as is it in the restaurants (possibly due to staff shortages), the drinks are mediocre, the rooms are spacious but uninspired, the facilities are showing their age and there doesn't seem to be any renovations planned anytime soon, and the food is nothing special. Honestly, I left with a bad taste in my mouth.

reviews.author: Antonio Osuna Cibrian
reviews.text: Excellent price for an all-inclusive, but all the lounge chairs and palapas were somewhat dirty and poorly arranged. I didn't like the warm beer, and the cocktails were terrible. Even so, the service was good, and the food was tasty. I'm giving it three stars because they wouldn't let us into the à la carte restaurant, even though they told us we could. They were even rude to us. Also, the executive parking lot is very fancy and covered, and they don't look after the guests as much.

reviews.author: Esau Lopez
reviews.text: For a hotel owned by the King and Queen of Spain, I expected more. The food was international, yes, but it lacked flavor and variety. The ocean-view rooms were nice, but the lagoon-view rooms were poorly maintained. The service at the pools is only good if you rent the lounge chairs! Overall, it's okay, but the price is very high for what you get!

reviews.author: Rene Gamez Handal
reviews.text: This time the experience was very different, as one security guard in particular overstepped his bounds, making us feel like we were going to steal something. He followed us all over the hotel because we were looking for someone who had told my parents she would put the wristbands on her desk for us, and he only stopped following us when we found her—because she wasn't at her desk. In the public areas, it's very annoying when the hotel vendors approach you and are so insistent, especially the one offering "free photo sessions." The service from the staff at the pool and restaurants, as always, is very friendly and good.

reviews.author: SONOTERAPIA Y SANACIÓN
reviews.text:
Rooms: Good, but not excellent. The closet door is a curtain, the air conditioning was very noisy (it's probably a very old unit), and the furniture looks dated. I'm being generous and giving it 4 stars.

Service: Average. It's common to have lines for breakfast and lunch at the buffet at certain times. This is the main restaurant, and they need more staff. It's normal for them to forget to bring your order, and the staff sometimes seems a bit overwhelmed. The stress makes the service good, but not excellent like at other resorts and cruises I've visited. It's not a 5-star hotel; I'd give it 3 stars.

On the beach, towels are sometimes unavailable. One day I couldn't shower because there weren't any towels, and another day I had to go to reception to complain, and they got me some.

If you're young, a young adult, or an adult with a youthful spirit, this is the most boring resort I've ever been to in Cancun and elsewhere. The shows are basic, there are no entertainers, no contests at night, no karaoke, and worst of all, at 11:30 PM there's nothing left to do but go to your room and sleep. The shows are low-quality and don't liven things up, and they usually end around 10:00 PM. The last time I was at Ryu Palace Peninsula, it set the bar much higher in terms of shows, entertainment, 24-hour bar service in the sports bar, and the shows lasted much longer. EASY 1:00 AM....THIS HOTEL IS VERY BORING FOR THOSE OF US WHO LIKE SHOWS AND A BOHEMIAN VIBE, IT DOESN'T EVEN HAVE A DISCO. I WOULDN'T RETURN, THERE ARE BETTER OPTIONS FOR A SIMILAR PRICE.

reviews.author: Xuanmei Jiang
reviews.text: The front desk service was very poor, but the other staff were friendly. The restaurant staff were friendly, but the food was not very tasty and served very slowly. The room was old and many of the facilities were malfunctioning, and the air conditioner didn't have a silent mode. The pool and bar were nice.

reviews.author: EZEQUIEL MEDEIROS
reviews.text:
The quality of service left much to be desired this time. The rooms smelled of mold and dampness, giving the impression that they had been closed up for a long time.

The service dropped considerably; we were poorly served by several employees, especially at breakfast. Abelardo was the exception at breakfast, always cheerful and courteous!

A shame, because the beach is excellent.

reviews.author: Lalo
reviews.text: It's a hotel that's already showing its age. I stayed there for six days, and on four of those nights, the maintenance staff started work at 11 p.m. Drills and hammers could be heard. I called the front desk to report the noise, but to no avail. I don't recommend Paradisus for a relaxing break. Getting the bill for your stay is a real challenge.

reviews.author: Manuel Moreno
reviews.text:
The hotel lobby is very nice. It's a shame it was under construction when I visited.
The staff, in general, are very friendly.

The entertainment could be improved, with more and better activities.
The rooms are somewhat dated and could use a renovation. The beds are comfortable.
Booking tours is cheaper if you book through an agency outside the hotel.

Upon arrival, a concierge is assigned to show you around the hotel and help with any questions. I asked for a special gift for my father's birthday, but they didn't do anything.

The best restaurants are Malva and Cappella. The others are nothing special.

Perhaps, for a hotel of this category, I expected a bit more.

reviews.author: Patricia Dallegri
reviews.text: The hotel is very beautiful but difficult to navigate. Lots of stairs everywhere. The service wasn't very good. They didn't restock the minibar. Anything you asked for was delayed or not done at all. The pools are very nice. The sea temperature is beautiful, but the sargassum is a nuisance. There's quite a lot of it. That's not the hotel's fault. When you arrive at the hotel, they charge you a $13 tax for sargassum cleanup. It's too much to control. If I return to Cancun, I wouldn't stay at this hotel again. But I must say, it is very beautiful.

reviews.author: Dario
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful. Unfortunately, when we went, three restaurants were closed, and they never informed us when we made the reservation, despite being a Circle Club member. They didn't give us the correct wristbands, which meant we were overcharged for the excursions we took (we didn't know they were supposed to give us a special wristband that gave us a 20% discount on paid events). For four nights, we had to eat hamburgers and fries by the pool because the hotel was packed for Thanksgiving, and with three restaurants closed, the lines for food were endless. The sales staff is very annoying, constantly following you around to try and sell you more packages. It really doesn't even come close to the Paradisus in Punta Cana. The staff at the hotel are good, depending on the shift you get. There were days when they offered drinks all the time by the pool, and other days when the waiter walked right past you without even asking if you wanted something. You're supposed to be paying for the service of being seated and having drinks offered to you constantly. The quality of the alcohol is excellent, with many brands and top-notch quality, nothing mediocre, that's truly wonderful... and the worst thing by far is the constant fight for the lounge chairs... we had to wake up at 7 a.m. to get a spot by the pool... it was a free-for-all every day. If you woke up at 9 a.m., you couldn't get a spot for the rest of the day. That's a very, very weak point...

reviews.author: Mayan Riviera Deluxe
reviews.text: I'll start with the positives: the staff is very attentive, especially the waiters and pool concierge. From the moment you arrive at the main entrance until you settle into a Balinese bed, the service is impeccable—very attentive and helpful. The reception area is small but practical and comfortable. The lobby is lovely, with a jungle-like touch that gracefully extends across all levels of the building and flows into artificial rivers where you can admire beautiful koi. The main pool is quite long, and the beach area is spacious, beautiful, and clean. On the downside, the shallow water makes the pool dangerous, as many children jump on the seats, and several slipped. I didn't see any lifeguards on the family side, but they arrived quickly when someone was injured. The water in the unheated pools was freezing. The breakfast buffet seems somewhat disorganized with the current situation regarding the virus; it's slow and inconvenient. It would be better to offer it à la carte. Ordering food and drinks at the pool also requires a lot of patience due to staff shortages, and the distances to get snacks are long if there are no servers. Finally, the food could be improved; it used to be good, not excellent, but it was good, and now it's fallen short. Sometimes it's not about having the most expensive cut of meat if they don't know how to prepare it; the seasoning is more important, and they should pay a little more attention to this.

reviews.author: Gonzalo. bm
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful, and the service was excellent at restaurants like Sal, Lemon Fish, and Malva. However, Blue Agave left much to be desired, both in terms of service—it seemed like everyone was angry—and in the food, which lacked both essential ingredients and flavor. The hotel is not recommended for older people because there's a lot of walking and several stairs. If you're staying in "The Reserve" area, be prepared to walk a lot, as all the restaurants are centrally located. There aren't enough carts to take you around, and there aren't enough restrooms because none of the restaurants have them; they're located outside the restaurants. If you like taking photos, the hotel has plenty of places to do so, and that's about it. 5/10

reviews.author: Siri Potluri
reviews.text:
Whilst the hotel is aesthetically pleasing, and in a great location (beach front), I personally wouldn’t visit again.

On paper there appears to be many restaurants for food choices, however you have to book well in advance to guarantee a place. The additional paying guests who are members of the Reserve get priority at most restaurants which is frustrating given others have also paid for all inclusive.

I felt the food at the restaurants was not good. Kau was good but others were not. The Italian restaurant especially served very bland food, and I ended up leaving how it is possible to make Italian food taste so bad. The dinner buffet is poor quality. So if you cannot reserve a table at the restaurants then you end of needing to go to the very poor buffet.

Most of the food in the restaurants (except kau) was either tasteless, overcooked, very odd taste or tiny portions.

Drinks options were good but no menus provided.

Pool was lovely but guests hog the sunbeds from around 08.00- they leave their towels there the whole day meaning by about 09.00 there is not a single sunbed left to use. On the beach we looked at hiring a beach bed, but it was 250 USD which is extortionate.

You cannot use the spa facilities like the steam room or sauna unless you book an extortionately priced massage or treatment.

The gym was good for a hotel gym.

I enjoyed the ice cream and the cafe.
I enjoyed the pool once i decided to give up on sunbed and use the patch of astroturf under a tree.

I reported a watch missing, and got security involved. All I wanted to know was whether they had cameras and whether somebody had entered my room when I was away. The security team searched our whole room, including our fridge, individual underwears, all corners of our suitcase. They also tried to search my parents rooms in the same manner, even though I told them I had definitely not visited there room and not lost my watch there. They then started to search my parents personal belongings including pill boxes etc. this was highly intrusive. I understand they have a policy to follow, but they did not listen I really don’t see the need for them go through my underwear….

All in all, I still had a good time but I enjoyed Cancun for the beautiful beaches, snorkelling, historical sites. I would not stay at Paradisus Cancun again.

reviews.author: Pete Papadopoulos
reviews.text:
The resort was recently remodeled and it just reopened about a week ago. I went there with my wife and two kids. The service was terrible. It was very slow. It took forever to check in. We were only there a few nights and we were unable to book any restaurants because they were "full", but half the tables in the restaurants were not filled.

The bathroom on floor 0 is disgusting and has a foul odor that you can smell from a distance from the bathroom.

Getting bottles of water from anywhere in the resort is impossible.They are either "out" at every bar or they just don't want to give it out.

The pools are nice and clean. The kid area is good. The food and drink service is awful. It takes forever to get drinks. While seated, you cannot order any food, you have to go to the snack shack, which serves burgers, tenders, fries, etc. The food was good, BUT you have to wait for over an hour in line to get the food because they have two people working the snack shack.

The hours of the bars, restaurants are awful.

We changed our flight and left early. Don't stay here.

reviews.author: Sandra Mohan
reviews.text:
I am writing this review 4 days after returning from our stay, and after reflecting on the experience, my opinion remains the same—disappointing.

My family and I regularly travel to Mexico, so we are well-seasoned travellers and understand what to expect from resorts at this level. Unfortunately, this resort fell short in several key areas.

Service was the biggest issue throughout our stay. Room service consistently took between 1 to 2.5 hours, and the policy of charging after a limited number of orders felt unreasonable. We also travelled with friends who experienced even worse delays, waiting over 5 hours for room service on one occasion. Housekeeping was average at best, and restocking of basic items like water, coffee, and snacks was inconsistent and often overlooked.

The room itself was underwhelming. The shower drain frequently clogged, causing unpleasant odors, and the overall space felt small and not well maintained.
Dining was mixed. The breakfast buffet was excellent, and the dinner buffet was also great. The Italian restaurant was a highlight of our stay. However, many items across other restaurants were unavailable, and vegetarian options were limited. Nighttime entertainment also did not meet expectations.

There were ongoing repairs during the day, and we encountered flooding in hallways without proper safety signage. On the fourth floor, there were severe ceiling leaks that created large puddles of water, posing a safety hazard for guests walking through the area.

Considering the premium price of this resort, this was unacceptable.
The hotel layout was confusing and made getting around inconvenient.
That said, there were some positives. The beach was well maintained with attentive beverage service, and the pools—especially the kids pool and swim-up pool—were excellent. The coffee shop and ice cream parlor were also standout features of the resort.

Tip for future guests: Poolside chairs are often taken very early (before 7:30am) with towels and then left unused, which is very frustrating—especially for families with young children who need seating. If your budget allows, consider renting a cabana (around $300). It’s covered, offers significantly better service, and includes food like lobster, shrimp skewers, fajitas, chips and dip, along with premium top-shelf drinks and consistent staff attention.

Overall, the lack of service, organization, and attention to detail significantly impacted our experience. Based on this stay, I would not recommend this resort.

reviews.author: Shaine Kumar
reviews.text:
I stayed at the Paradisus in Cancun for five days (February 1–6, 2025) with my girlfriend, family, and friends.

Positives: The beach is a highlight—spacious and enjoyable. The swim-up bar bartender was attentive and friendly, adding to the relaxed vibe. The buffet restaurant stood out as well, offering good food quality and a decent selection compared to other dining options.

Negatives: We paid for a Family Concierge Ocean View room, but upon arrival, we were assigned a bottom-floor room in Pyramid 3 with no view of the water at all. Despite complaining to the front desk, we received no resolution or assistance.

The restaurants, aside from the steakhouse, were disappointing. Service was consistently slow, and the food quality was subpar. I wouldn’t recommend booking most of the à la carte restaurants; I’d have preferred sticking to the buffet every night.

To make matters worse, on the second-to-last night, $100 CAD was stolen from our room—presumably by housekeeping. The money was in my girlfriend’s wallet, zipped inside another bag within a backpack. While it was our fault for not using the room safe, the incident was incredibly disappointing. We reported it to hotel security and staff, who promised to follow up after their investigation, but we never heard back—complete radio silence.

I won’t be returning to this property on my next visit to Cancun and will take my business elsewhere.

reviews.author: Eileen Conton
reviews.text: I’m going to start by saying the hotel is beautiful. Do i recommend it? No, i’ll tell you why… Is an expensive hotel and we received the worse service. If you did not booked the concierge experience they treat you like you are nobody, they try to force you to get the package with the concierge and once you say no the black list you. Without that package you have to make a line to make reservations on the restaurants. Once you try to make reservations for the restaurants they tell you they are all booked so you can get frustrated and upgrade your package to concierge package. They leave the restaurant reservations for those with the upgrade. The restaurants could be empty but they’ll tell you is all booked, i know because i watched all night how tables were empty and they do not accept walk ins (when you pay your money to eat good). I was able to go to one of the restaurants there and the food was disgusting. A I had to go outside the hotel every night for dinner because the hotel i payed for all inclusive did not have a table for me in any restaurant on the premises.  Overall, this place is just good for pictures, if you are trying to book a hotel with good food and experience this is not it. Do not recommend it.

reviews.author: Cameryn Porter Choate
reviews.text:
We stayed 5 nights here last week. The experience was very hit and miss. We did two days at the pool on the adults only (reserve) side of the resort in reserved Bali beds. The first day we had excellent service and were very happy! The gal waiting on us checked on us frequently. The second day we spent in the reserved Bali bed we were checked on very little, had to retrieve drinks from the bar as waiter wasn't coming around frequently, ordered lunch through the app for the same reason, and at one point the staff had congregated directly by our bed and were chatting for several minutes which was a bit awkward. During that same day a staff member was literally painting the base of the Bali bed as we were laying in it... not very comfortable!

The buffet food was just okay. Some things better than others... some staff friendlier than others as well. The restaurant experience was much better with the exception of our dinner at Cielo which was not the best. Food wasn't great and service was very slow and Cielo. Sante was fantastic for both breakfast and dinner and Sal was great as well! Cappella was great service too!

Communication wasn't great. We were told our concierge would reach out quickly after checking in to assist us with reservations. We didn't hear from him until about 2pm on our second day and many of the restaurants book out days in advance so our reservation options were limited to what was available. When we didn't hear from the concierge in a timely fashion we were able to find a reservation table with staff members to assist us.

Rooms were okay! Not super noteworthy but worked for us. Shower and tub are nice. Walls are super thin, we heard a lot from our neighbors. We did find out from one of the staff members that the hotel is closing down in May and will be closed for a year as they complete major renovations. This makes sense considering a lot of the resort was in need of some attention. The resort is beautiful and photographs nicely but could definitely benefit from some renovations. It rained one day and the inside of the resort had  towels placed everywhere I assume because of leaks in the building.

Jesus from Cappella was amazing! He recommended the tagliata di manzo al rosmarino to my husband and it was delicious! 10/10 service and great food, beverage, and atmosphere! Highly recommend!

reviews.author: Khodadad Javaheri
reviews.text:
Our stay at Paradisus Cancun was unfortunately far below what we expected from a five-star all-inclusive hotel. While there were some positives, significant issues greatly impacted our experience.

Positives:
•	Beautiful beach: The beachfront was stunning and well-maintained.
•	Large, clean pool: The pool area was enjoyable and offered a relaxing atmosphere.
•	Friendly and helpful staff: The servers and bartenders were particularly kind and attentive, enhancing the dining and bar experience.

Negatives:
1.	Maintenance Issues:
•	We experienced a ceiling leak in our bathroom that required multiple follow-ups to address.
•	When we requested a resolution, we were told we could upgrade to a renovated oceanfront room for $100 extra instead of having the problem fixed promptly. This approach felt opportunistic and inappropriate given the circumstances.
2.	Cleanliness Problems:
•	We saw small roaches 3 times: once in the restaurant on the ground, once in our hotel room on the ground, and once in the hotel room drawer where clothes were stored.
•	We also found a dying bug inside the fridge in our room, which was highly unpleasant and concerning.
•	These cleanliness issues are unacceptable for a five-star property.
3.	Outdated Rooms:
•	The rooms felt old and in need of renovation. This detracted from the overall experience.
4.	Food Quality:
•	Across all restaurants, the food was bland and uninspiring, not meeting the standards expected at this price point.
5.	Missed Room Cleaning:
•	Room cleaning was missed entirely on one day of our stay.
6.	Weak Entertainment Options:
•	The entertainment was underwhelming, with short and unengaging events. Many evenings, we found ourselves unsure of how to spend our time due to a lack of compelling activities.

Overall, while the beach, pool, and staff were lovely, these positives could not outweigh the significant shortcomings in maintenance, cleanliness, and food quality. The experience was well below five-star standards, and we would not consider returning.

reviews.author: Angelica Escobedo
reviews.text: Overpriced compared to other nearby resorts. Rooms are dated, raggedy & beds uncomfortable and leg to bed about to fall off. Common areas and restaurants are remodeled. Food is ok, drinks were good, service was great. Huge inconvenience in allowing people to reserve all the spots on the beach, they should be first come first serve. Beach and water were great,  end of Feb. Not worth going back.

reviews.author: Ronya Buzbee
reviews.text: The room was small, but clean.  Some flying bugs but I imagine the environment makes it hard to control those.  Staff was very friendly and location was in great proximity to airport.  Food was mediocre at best.  We tried all the restaurants and were not impressed at all by any of them.  The biggest issue though was with the pools. It was either 5-6ft depth or 2ft depth. This is difficult if you have a 7 year old who is not a strong swimmer but way too big for the 2ft baby pool. We always either had to be in the pool with her or had to watch her every second.  I would not recommend this resort to families with elementary aged children.  And I have a major issue with the cleanliness of the pools. Four days into our trip my daughter got hand foot mouth disease.  I am 100% sure she got it from the pool.  Main pool with the swim up bar specifically.  Always noticed things floating on top but assumed it was safe and treated with the necessary chemicals.  Not the case. You need to check your chlorine levels and sanitize.  Super grossed out by this.

reviews.author: Wealthy CM
reviews.text: We went at Paradisus through Sunwing and booked the ocean front king room but they gave us double bed room which we said we cannot have this for entire week stay. They said they only have this room for a night and can come back tomorrow to check if king bed room is available which we did and they provided a king room but with not great ocean view which was disappointing since we paid premium price for this.During our stay we felt very much racism from all of the servers and bar tenders. They were not giving any attention to what we ask and do not answer our questions. I also want to shout out to one of the bartender who was very rude and he mixed multiple alcohol in our drink when we just asked for one. This bartender was at the pool bar where there is sitting in the water at the bar. Restaurant are not that great and nobody was attending us and ignoring us more.
