We then go to Agua Mariana to have our main course but again, we wasted 45 minutes at Agua Mariana just for a soup again. So we decided to go back to our room. We still have 2 days left here but we will just order in room services and pay extra to not waste our time. I will also advise my friend to consider this for their upcoming trips to Cancun.

reviews.author: Cessar Solano
reviews.text: Staff is what stands out, property needs some work and food could definitely be better. Big shout out to everyone who works there, special thanks to limberth butler, Victor and David pool concierge, waiting staff is sante and atrio section Oscar, César, Lorena, Luis and Alejandro in the bar are the best!

reviews.author: Stavo P
reviews.text: I will start by saying the hotel is beautiful and was great in location. However we paid extra for “the reserve” which we thought would be adults only and exclusive from children. We had stayed before when the reserve was royal service and had tower 5 for the reserve/royal service specifically. Tower 5 was for everyone including children. Our room was in the main tower also with children. We paid the extra for the reserve and adults only however the only thing we got adults only was the pool. Not impressed. Don’t waste your money for the reserve it’s not worth it. Other then that food was great. Adults only pool was great. Very relaxed and quiet. Staff was great. George our concierge was nice and reserved us Bally beds for the days we were there. Didn’t see him much which was ok. Nicole/Nikki at the adults only pool was amazing!

reviews.author: T E (TinManWarrior)
reviews.text: Place was nice but hot, no AC in the main lobby, which made it feel you are in a greenhouse (very humid, and hot). The hotel leaks so be prepared to see buckets everywhere, the bath tub had a crack, the balcony would flood and not drain the water out every time it rained, and there was a lot of roaches that we encountered, even at the buffet, and our room. I give it 3 stars because the service was good, and the people where nice, and the beach area was great! I think it can be better, but definitely a 3 star hotel.

reviews.author: Hamed Mahmoudi
reviews.text:
My recent stay at Paradisus Cancún was unfortunately far from the 5-star experience I anticipated. Here are some key issues I encountered during my visit:

1. Delayed Check-In:
Despite the advertised check-in time of 3 PM, I didn't receive my room until 3:45 PM. This delay set the tone for a series of disappointments.

2. Room Quality:
Upon entering the room, I expected a luxurious, 5-star environment as advertised. However, I was greeted with a cracked sink, a mirror that was fading at the corners, and a shower that felt more akin to a budget motel than a premium resort.

3. Dining Challenges:
Getting food was a major hassle. There was a one-hour waiting list just to dine, making the buffet the only viable option. Even the buffet had a long line in the morning, taking about an hour to get in. Additionally, the service was subpar; it took 20 minutes for servers to return with coffee refills.

4. Pool and Beach Facilities:
The pool area was overcrowded with a limited number of lounge chairs. Unless you secured a spot very early in the morning, finding a chair was impossible. On a positive note, the beach was relatively clean with an adequate number of lounge chairs available.

5. Dinner Wait Times:
Dinner was another disappointment with a two-hour waiting list after 8 PM. This added unnecessary stress to what should have been a relaxing experience.

6. Not Kid-Friendly:
Additionally, this resort is not kid-friendly. There were not many activities for children, making it difficult to keep them entertained.

I visited Paradisus Cancún a few years ago and had an amazing experience, but sadly, the quality has significantly declined. If you are looking for a true 5-star quality hotel, I recommend considering other options. This experience was highly disappointing, and I will not be returning.

I hope this review helps others who are seeking a quality vacation and a resort where they can fully enjoy their time with their family.

reviews.author: Sabrina
reviews.text:
My first time with Royal Service but my second at Paradisus. Our butler, Alain, was less than helpful. We spent our very short trip doing most things on our own. Hector wasn't even our butler but he tried to help us as much as possible. He was great and is the only reason I would even remotely consider Royal Service again. If it weren't for Hector, I would never book Royal service again.
The room was great and most of the other staff were amazing. The spa comes highly recommended. Ana there is the best.
Daphne at the concierge desk in Royal Service was very pushy. I didn't expect to be hounded about taking a "tour" that I had been on before. I told her no once but that wasn't enough. The sales pitch became really old after just 2 short days.

reviews.author: Cecily Shi
reviews.text:
Pro: beautiful beach, pool. Staffs at the restaurant and bars are amazing! Their activities staffs are so helpful and friendly.  Food is amazing at the buffet and at all of the restaurants.
Con: big problems during checking in for my friend, she has to go to front desk for 4 times to get her bracelet key working. We had two rooms, but were separated in different t floors when they actually have a ton of availabilities of rooms right next to each other.  They need upgrade their front desk services in order to be a 5 star hotel.   Also, big problems with reserving restaurants.   Noisy constructions going on, I wish guests would receive some bonus for living through dusts and noises during the stay.  The room is definitely out of dated- lights not working, shower not working correctly.  Very noisy at the pool during the day where some guests brought their own speaker- hope they control the music and noise level a bit more towards international guests.

reviews.author: Rachel Kellam
reviews.text:
Paradisus was awesome for our family trip over the new year holiday! We saw alot of pros and cons, will list them below.

Restaraunts: We didn't have any wait at any of the restaraunts like other reviews mentioned. I'm not sure if we just showed up at a good time. Almost all the food was pretty mediocre, there were just 1 or 2 dishes the entire trip that were slam dunk amazing but the rest was basically edible. I was also quite sad at the lack of true Mexican food.

Service:
- Miguel at the reserve pool was 10/10 and absolutely made our trip phenomenal. He was super friendly, accommodating, and happy to help us where ever we were on the resort (whether at a different pool on the reserve side, beach etc.). He was great and even went beyond to offer us some of the room service menu poolside.
- Abel, our concierge was 1/10. After the first day he basically vanished, took forever to respond to any requests, he also at times gave us straight incorrect information (ex: we asked to reserve a cabana, he said they were full but we were able to go up and just reserve it ourselves.). He would promise to do big things and never followup (ex. Giving my mom a surprise for her birthday that never happened. Promising he would go get us a chess set "right now" and after we waited for him for an hour we figured he was never coming back). He was super misinformed about NYE so we missed out on the NYE dinner that the resort was hosting. I'm not quite sure what happened / if it was just a bad week but we definitely navigated the resort better after just bypassing our concierge.

Resort: The resort was phenomenal was SO MUCH beach access. We were never uncomfortable and everyone in the family was able to enjoy what they wanted whether it be in pool lounges, a deeper pool, swimming in the ocean, laying in the cabanas or beaches. For relaxing the resort was amazing. If you're looking for a crazy party I would go elsewhere or only come to this resort when a big event is happening like a festival. It's pretty laid back and chill (even on NYE)

Overall 3/5 stars because even given some of the downsides, we had such an amazing time. The resort was beautiful, had wonderful beach access and a great place to connect with family.

reviews.author: Shivani Karia
reviews.text:
This hotel was chosen by my family for a number of reasons. 1) It was extremely highly rated on both Google and TripAdvisor. Received, for the most part, a number of really great, high reviews. 2) It was said to have a number of kids activities, including a splash pad for kids. 3) The site stated that there are 18 restaurants, bars, cafes with exceptional dining.

Unfortunately, this is not a resort I will return to, and here are the reasons why:

1) Dining. The food was mediocre at best. In Malva, which is the buffet, the food was not fresh, it served the exact same things every day, and there were very, very few proper vegetarian options. The pancakes weren't cooked all the way through, the pasta sauce was way too watery, and not everything had labels, so it was hard to discern between different sauces and foods. Which, leads to my next point. This resort offers only 1-2 vegetarian options in each of their restaurants. Their "restaurant concierge" was not able to help us find anything vegetarian-friendly, and basically told us "mm yeah you gotta talk to the chefs." Even the italian restaurant had limited options, too. We were able to go to one of the Spanish restaurants (Blue Agave) and thankfully their ONLY two vegetarian options were tasty, but that was it. We (understandably) knew that we wouldn't be eating at the steakhouse, but in this day and age, to not have vegetarian options is a HUGE miss. Poolside, the only vegetarian options were fries and nachos. So yeah. Wonderful.

2) Kids' activities. We checked out the kids' club once when, according to the website there was a friendship bracelet making activity scheduled. Well, turns out the website schedule was wrong. Thankfully the staff there was super sweet and they still let my daughter make a bracelet. We also expected a proper kids' splash pad and pool with toys and activities, and all it was was a shallow pool. There were no toys, activities, splash pad, etc. If you're coming to this resort expecting slides and a splash pad for the kids, DON'T. There are much better options.

So while the food and the kids activities were a huge huge miss, i do want to call out the staff, who were all super kind, welcoming and sweet throughout our entire stay. The only one whose name I remember unfortunately is Beatriz from the pool staff who was an absolute sweetheart. The others were, too! I just can't remember their names.

We also had to call the resort's doctor on staff, Dr. Adrian and he was super helpful and comforting. He spoke extremely clearly, was very kind and reassuring and we felt comfortable with him.

Overall, I don't think we'll come back to this resort again, unfortunately.

reviews.author: Jane C
reviews.text:
The pictures of Paradisus don't lie - the resort is every bit as lush, well-kept, and luxurious as displayed. Housekeeping and maintenance staff work around the clock to ensure everything stays that way, and we were impressed by their obvious diligence to upkeep the physical property.

That said, there were some clear cons. I'm surprised to see no one mentioning the lack of air conditioning at this resort. The main areas and many of the restaurants are NOT kept cool, which made our July stay fairly uncomfortable for heat-intolerant members of our family. The glass ceilings in the main part of the resort, along with the beautiful greenery, created a humid greenhouse effect that left us hibernating in the few temperature-controlled areas on the resort - namely our suite, the buffet area, and the single bar that had offered a/c. So word to the wise, if keeping cool during the summer months is important to you.

Our assigned suite had a faulty HVAC system, and trying to get our room changed required three trips to the check-in area on the very first day. There was a wait on a line each time, and while we were able to eventually get our room changed, we certainly didn't expect to expend nearly an hour and a half of our trip on that endeavor.

The food was just all right. The buffet recycled many of the same tired options throughout our meals during the week. They've done away with the reservation system for the restaurants, but the first-come, first-served system now means long wait times for tables. Cappellus (sp? the Italian restaurant) was our family's clear favorite, and I wish we would've spent more of our time there than waiting hours for some disappointing fare at other places.

For much of our trip, I found myself dodging conversations with the concierge and staff. What first seemed warm and welcoming would quickly become an invitation to enjoy special gifts or free spa care...for a time cost of sitting through a timeshare promotion (or what they now call 'vacation packages'). I have no qualms about saying 'no' to the occasional offer, but it didn't feel great to be approached that way on a near daily basis.

The clear highlight of the trip were our servers. They are earnest, efficient, and helpful. Joni at the buffet and Aurelio at the Italian restaurant were amazing, and paid such care and attention to what we needed.

For the cost, I didn't feel Paradisus was worth the while, particularly during the hottest season of the year.

reviews.author: Jayden Bardwell
reviews.text: The experience was nice however the first day my family and I were met with not so pleasant employees ignoring us. We made sure to be respectful and friendly but a few days later some items from my room went missing. Not only in my room but in a room where my other family stayed as well. I was quite disappointed because I know exactly where I put my cologne which was expensive and it was gone along with some other items.

reviews.author: Dude
reviews.text: Ok, this is more a good 4 star hotel. Food is just ok, do not think blue agave, lemon, and other restaurants really stand out. Unfortunately service and attention to latin and mexican people is not good. I was in playa del carmen paradisus and was much better experience. I dont think ill comeback to this one...ever.

reviews.author: B M
reviews.text:
We have been here for a week now. This is my impression.
Old but beautiful hotel, clean. Most of the staff is pleasant. The best one is the always smiling and pleasant guy from the coffee shop.
The food is mediocre. We are the crowd of 12 ppl who travel all over the world- nothing wrong with our pallets (before the  management sarcastically replies) who are accustomed eating all world’s cuisines and none of us liked the food here except: the tacos by the pool, paella by the pool, pizza by the pool and ceviches at the restaurants and some of the foods at Blue Agave.
Almost all food lack seasoning. I felt I was on a renal diet all week long.
This place doesn’t represent well amazing Mexican cuisine.
We booked king bed, they gave us two full beds. The matress size was full and frame possible queen but two of us slept on a full all week. It was not pleasant especially after burning in the sun.

The pools are nice.
My complaint is about the washing of the cups/ glasses . Almost every glass I had was dirty as they dip it in the soapy water and rinse it but don’t wash around. Not hygienic at all. No sanitizers around.

Also, even with the all inclusive package they are not giving u bottled water at the pool bars, those are reserved exclusively for the folks with cabanas so if have sensitive stomachs u can’t get bottled water. U have to drink tap water which is ridiculous for $450 plus rooms per nights. I don’t drink alcohol but I drink plain water and for my $450 all inclusive per night I want to be able to have bottled water!
I also saw hair strands in the basket of churros as well around the platters. The churros outside over the weekend were delicious.
Saw roaches outside of my room roaming.
If I ever return it will be for the good vibes, churros by the pool, location and Daisy.

There is a cat Daisy at the resort by the pool area.Feel free to feed this poor soul and give her water as they do nothing about her. She is there as a circus monkey to be admired by the guests but the management does nothing for her.
Daisy currently has upper respiratory infection and that was reported to the management but they care less to take her to the vet😡heartless ppl..

When I get assurance that you guys took care of Daisy I will remove this portion of my review.

reviews.author: victor demattos
reviews.text:
My family stayed at Paradisus for a week-long trip. This trip has been overall a mixed bag. The resort itself is lovely, the pseudo eco-brutalism design esthetic is very appealing and works well with the overall environment. The pool area as well as the restaurants are all very beautiful and lend to a luxurious feeling to the resort.
Unfortunately this is where that luxury ends my party was made up of three individual rooms, one of the three rooms experienced major plumbing issues both with the sinks and with the showers/bath. Including rust on various parts of the bath and a shower head that was coming detached, as well as a clogged sink drain. Another major issue that came up not only for the room with the plumbing issues but for another room on the other side of the resort was roaches. The room with the plumbing issue had one large roach and the other room had not only one large roach in the bathroom but also four smaller roaches climbing in and around the central entertainment center area which included the mini fridge, which I might add is your only way of accessing drinking water in the rooms.
This issue was brought up to reception and both rooms were able to get switched with minimal hassle. However, the staff were seemingly totally unsympathetic (When told about the room with the plumbing issues and the roach staff asked if we wanted the room cleaned, we then had to request a room change.) never even offering an apology for the incident and seeming almost annoyed at the fact that we were requesting a room change.  To be as fair as possible on some degree, it is not entirely surprising to find roaches in a large resort in a semi-tropical climate, however my entire party and I felt that the way we had to go about getting things changed was not adequate. I work retail, I know how annoying and difficult customers can be. The service industry is tough, especially in tourist areas like Cancun. However, the issues we faced and the way the reception handled it in our opinion soured the entire experience. I don’t think guests should be treated like a burden when bringing up legitimate health and safety concerns.
On a better note I do want to give credit where credit is due, the vast majority of the servers and attendants at the resort were absolutely wonderful. They were helpful, kind, and seemed to honestly care about giving the guest a favorable experience. The food was also another highlight, variety was through the roof and just about every dish we ate was cooked beautifully and tasted fantastic (although do be warned they do go light on the salt.)
Overall as I stated at the beginning of this review are stay was a mixed bag, the “resort” experience was good and genuinely very enjoyable, however the more “hotel” aspect of the trip was quite possibly the worst I have ever had. Overall, I cannot recommend staying at this resort. Everything about your stay might be fantastic but with a nearly 2/3 chance of landing yourself in a room with roaches, why take this risk when Cancun as a number of wonderful roach free resorts to stay at.

reviews.author: Shreshth Luthra
reviews.text:
It’s our first time in Cancun and Paradisus. We came here to celebrate our anniversary with very high hopes. This place met some of other hopes but not others

1. Room service is not so good. They take atleast 40 mins just to deliver water bottles

2. Food is not great. Everyone raves about lemon fish but it was terrible. Dry sushi and super dry salmon with rice. I am not going there again

3. For most part, service in restaurants is good. Restaurant staff is courteous

4. They have a bunch of good entertainment events happenings throughout the week. Best was the silent disco.

reviews.author: Brian Mach
reviews.text:
Communication is key! Upon checking in, seeing that one of us uses a cane and would need access to an elevator, we were assigned a room in Pyramid 1, the furthest building from the main Pyramid, on the 4th floor. Upon making it to Pyramid 1, we were informed the elevator was broken. Why wouldn't the front desk know this? We had to walk back and request a different room. While we were accommodated, we shouldn't have had to do this in the first place.

We found our room clean for the most part. However, all of the vents were covered in a decent layer of dust. In fact, every vent we saw through out the resort was covered in dust. Also of note was the absence of the bidet in the restroom. It had clearly recently been removed and we were left wondering as to why.

Service was wonderful at the pool side bar, the pool area, and especially at Melva. The buffet at Melva was the best. Agua Marina left much to be desired for the service as well as the food. Blue Agave service was incredibly slow, however the food was delicious.

We did like how close this resort was to the airport. It made for a quick commute. The complex is showing it's age, and needs updating. It appears the owners are trying to upgrade the property around the guests. One day, the common area was filled with smoke and diesel fumes from renovations. We thought we would need to evacuate as the haze did enter our room.

If you are considering this resort, keep in mind it is quite large. It consists of 5 Pyramids, with the 3rd Pyramid as the main building, all connected on the main floor. It was too large and spread out for us.

Overall, we did enjoy our stay in paradise. But we will choose a different resort next time.

reviews.author: Luca Riccardi
reviews.text: Hotel is very nice, all inclusive, great restaurants, but they also have weak points! First of all they close all the bars at 11pm, which is way too early, so if you want to enjoy a drink after dinner you cannot. I was in Paradisus of other locations and they still served drinks even night time, so I don't understand why here in Cancun they close so early. Secondly the reception is too small for such a big hotel, so every time at the reception there is a long queue and it takes for ever to get your turn. Overall for an all inclusive resort it's worth it, but some things can be improved. I give 3 stars because if i compare to Paradisus in Playa del Carmen or the ones in Spain I've been to, this is below them.

reviews.author: Brian Stout (Brian)
reviews.text: The night club across the street plays loud music throughout the night on the bayside. The restaurant service was good especially the italian place. The seaweed was handled good. It is not all inclusive as the steak and lobster were extra charge. The drinks seemed to be weak in my opinion. Its a 3 star maybe 4 at best. Nice but we got sick. Mediocre!

reviews.author: A Johnson
reviews.text:
Many issues on this trip, probably not enough space here to describe them all. It shouldn't have been possible to be disappointed with the ocean right there, but still somehow it happened.

The app never worked for us, despite reinstalling it and trying it on a different phone - even when logged in with our Melia account, we would search for our stay and it would say it was saved, then when selecting My Stay it said we had no stays. Spoke with multiple resort employees about this, including Aaron our assigned concierge, and yet no one could fix it. Because of this we couldn't use our coupons/promos and missed out on experiences we wanted to have.

When booking, my 14-yr-old was considered an adult, and we paid extra for The Reserve upgrade because we wanted access to the private pool. Imagine our disappointment when we were informed we couldn't be in the pool area because she wasn't 18. Furthermore there were no cabanas available in the entire resort until the day of our departure, although there were lesser cabanas without services on the beach they wanted $200/day for.

The non-Reserve area is very loud and crowded, with irritating EDM pumping constantly. It was absolutely not the relaxing beach experience we were looking for from this caliber of resort. We finally just took our towels and sat on the beach.

Because the app didn't work, we weren't able to review restaurant info or book reservations without walking to a tiny table on the other side of the resort which took three separate inquiries to find. We ate mostly at the buffet in pyramid 5 (which was small but really wonderful), and ordered room service -- which was an embarrassment. The lobster eggs Benedict, which we paid an extra fee for, was awful. One of the eggs was undercooked and inedible, while the lobster was overcooked and rubbery.

Aaron proactively booked dinner for us at two different restaurants; one was an absolutely incredible meal we will remember for years to come, while the other had mediocre service and none of our food arrived hot (even the ice cream on my daughter's dessert was melting by the time it reached us). I don't understand how these two completely opposite experiences happened at the same resort.

The room was very comfortable, except the lounge chair in our room was broken when we arrived. I mentioned this to Aaron and nothing was done about it. Also, the bathrooms have been retrofitted with glass walls to give the illusion of more space. While this is a good design choice, it was very awkward not having much privacy while showering -- all there is between the shower and the room is a clear glass wall and a thin gauze curtain. This would be fine for couples traveling, but for my daughter and I in a room with separate beds it was uncomfortable, so FYI if you are not on a romantic getaway.

reviews.author: RR2887
reviews.text:
The resort is beautiful! Great view to the ocean! Great restaurants and great staff for the most part (Lemon Fish and Cielo are probably the best restaurants)

Room: 1/5:
unfortunately, the rooms are not nearly as great as the outside. Peeling paint, shabby bathroom, leaking roof.. so our room experience wasn’t the greatest.

Kinsdom Review (by my daughter)5/5:
The Kidsdom activity helpers are nice and friendly to the kids who need help and are always available for any questions. They are also very kind. They always have great activities to keep everyone happy and busy. Even if children don’t know what to do multiple times they are always happy to help. Rubi ,Sheila,Bruno,Monse,Tranna and Ivonne are all very nice people who have a great talent of helping kids. I have had a lot of great memories with Kidsdom and I am so grateful to have been able to meet everyone at Kidsdom and I am so thankful to have had a chance to be in Kidsdom. I will always remember the memories of Kidsdom and the staff. I will miss being in kidsdom and being able to meet the staff.
I hope that we can meet again.

Outdoor photography: 5/5: you must get an outdoor photoshoot done as it’s a great memory of your vacation! Oscar from the outdoor shoot is amazing and so are his subordinates!!

In the end, we carry a lot of fond memories from the resort and thank the staff for making our stay enjoyable.

reviews.author: Delbert Matlock
reviews.text: The hotel needs some renovation. Rooms are worn, and my AC sounded like it in had a can of rocks in it. Several complaints to the front desk didn't help. Food quality was not what I had hoped. Even the specialty restaurants were hit or miss. Building itself is amazing. The hollow pyramids with lots of fountains and plants is very pleasant.

reviews.author: Anny Kach
reviews.text:
GINGER Bar. THE BEST BARTENDERS.... BALTAZAR ,LUZ ,GLADIS, ERICK they were honestly the highlight of my trip.

FRANCESCO  WAITER BEACH WAS AWESOME 👌 SUPER FAST AND HELPFUL

reviews.author: Sushmita Tiwari
reviews.text: We booked our stay at The Reserve (Adult) the views were stunning and so the restaurant Sante was really good. We even enjoyed the Bracelet activity, Housie , Key chain making with Santi. That guy is too good and helped us to know more about the resort. We even did a pottery session with Happyfaces_Cancun and painting the animals was fun. We even enjoyed the Hydro therapy and massage session by Ashanti and her partner name Loue ( I dnt remember her name correctly) We even did the photo session with outdoor photography.In terms of Vegetarian options Sante & Malva had few options which are liked by us. Flora’s Spinach pasta was awesome. The staff of Sante were very welcoming and helped a lot with vegetarian food and drinks. The only issue we found was in the rooms. Shower area water was coming out from there and was all over the place. The toilet was jammed and so was very difficult 😞 Won’t recommend for staying but for Sante food with the views  and massage you can definitely try.

reviews.author: Heather Tomaino
reviews.text: Food was okay, room was okay. The people were great. Especially Axcel in activities. My kids had so much fun! Our Reserve concierge did little to help us out. We saw him maybe twice when we were there. I wouldn't upgrade to Reserve again, but the staff and pool and ocean were great!

reviews.author: David Osborne
reviews.text: So we and my lady recently traveled here and our room was very out dated, so we upgraded to VIP building 5 ocean view. Which was a bit better, but really just painted over furniture. The concierge you’ve paid for isn’t available 24/7. You also get hustled into a time share meeting. I didn’t know what the conversation was going to be but was told they wanted 30 minutes of my time but it took 2 hours out of our vacation. The hotel was empty and yet was difficult to get dinner reservations with our concierge trying to book it. The resort outside of the room was very nice, the decorum was amazing. For those leaving to airports an Uber is $16 and the taxis the hotel call charge $45 #highway robbery. All inclusive wasn’t true, as VIP members were allowed in Sals restaurant but the good meals all came with an extra cost out of pocket. Staff was friendly but we’ll never return again.

reviews.author: mike multani
reviews.text: Hotel entrance beautiful!! In my room there was big crack on the marble ( they had marble installed on the table ) i spoke with someone in the lobby about it, they told me they will change our room but they never did Later twice I was trying to speak with the  manager ( marisol) she was in the back room never showed up ! …. Angelica ( supervisor) told me that they will charge all the kids 5 yr n above !! My daughter was 4 they still charged ( I was so tired and don’t want to argue for 300$ ) . Except lobby all the rest of staff were amazing always serve you with beautiful smile . But never again !!!! HARD ROCK is much better

reviews.author: Octavio Gonzalez
reviews.text: We had a lot of issues with our reservation.   All issues were internal!  Rooms are good.  Restaurants are good, not great!  Especially with the cost.  You have to make all reservations with a phone app, unfortunately the app does not work well.  The beaches are in bad shape.  They try to clean as much as possible, but it's impossible to keep it clean.  The staff are great, polite and helpful.

reviews.author: Mo Kak
reviews.text:
Good things - Staff was nice. Cabana set up towards the beach was lovely.

The bad - The Reserve is billed as the ADULTS ONLY section of the resort. At one point it was that and it still says it is on the site. IT’S NOT! Not sure if the pandemic forced them to stop the adults only section but there are families and kids everywhere, including the pools and restaurants that are supposed to be reserved for adults. If that doesn’t bother you then cool but if you’re going off of what the website says just know that is no longer the case.

Food was hit or miss with the restaurants. Some were good others missed the mark.

reviews.author: David Dinan
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed in the Royal Service, building 5. Overall it really was a very nice stay. Great food, very relaxing, just what we were looking for. Unfortunately, we had a major issue at checkout. They wouldn't let us leave without waiting in a long line to physically check out. They stopped us as we were walking out the door and said we weren't permitted to leave until we checked out. I told them my room number and said they had my credit card on file and just to charge the card for any additional charges. They repeated that we were not permitted to leave the resort until we checked out. So my wife and I stood in a long line that wasn't moving for about 5 minutes and after seeing the line not move I told the same person again that we were leaving and to charge my card for any extras. He repeated that we would not be permitted to leave. I said that I didn't think they'd stop us and we loaded our bags into the car that we had hired. Sure enough, a hotel rep came outside and told the driver he wasn't permitted to leave with us because we had not checked out. Our driver would not drive. We were actually being held by the hotel until we waited in there ridiculous line to say that we were leaving on the same day that our reservation said.  Ultimately we walked back to building 5 where the line was shorter and we checked out there.
The check in process at this hotel took too long (and they are aggressive about trying to sell you a timeshare while you check-in) and the idea that we had to physically check out of the hotel just doesn't make sense to me. Nice vacation, but after the check out experience, we'll never go back to this resort.

reviews.author: Jessica Hamilton
reviews.text: Been twice to this locaion. Great location close to the international airport. Polite and friendly service. Things are clean but my rooms have been run down.

reviews.author: C Park
reviews.text:
Stayed here in June of 2019.
Here are my observations:

Facilities: Great
Notes: Very humid and hot in common areas
- Baby room: can leave your infant there if they are over a year old and can stand by themselves.  Staff mainly just turn on the tv and let the kids watch.  My infant picked up hand, foot, mouth disease from their kids area.
- Decently fast wifi
- Lots of activities
- Bars everywhere.
- Quite a few huts for shade by the pool. You can also rent one of the bali beds for $. Didn't do it so not sure how much it is. But they do have electrical outlets built into each bali bed too so you can charge your devices.

Room: Junior Suite Ocean View - Good
Notes:
- View - beautiful
- Balcony - private and great shade
- No coffee maker for warming baby bottle
- Mini fridge - canned beer, pop, juice boxes and bottles of water
- Sheets are nice and soft
- A/C is strong but loud
- Hallway noise is loud
- Outside nightly performance is really loud

Food: Good
We tried every restaurant but the paid one. They were all ok. Not the greatest but better than passable.  It was too hot to eat breakfast at the buffet so we gave up after the 3/4th day and instead just ordered room service.  Pretty sure the room service fruit gave us all mild food poisoning.  I know it's the fruit because that was the only thing my daughter ate of our food.  She had severe diarrhea for 24 hours, which luckily went away just in time for our flight.
Bana one was ok. I did enjoy their octopus and sea bass sashimi. Everything else was only so-so.
The restaurants book up quickly, you pretty much have to book two days in advance. There's an app of theirs you can download to request bookings but then you end up having this back and forth because you can only request a booking without seeing actual availabilities.
Blue agave was a disappointment.
At Vento we ordered about 7/8 dishes, and 2 of them were good, can't remember which ones they were anymore.
Didn't try Enso at night. Checked out their menu. Looks like it would be a disappointment. Weird choice of dishes.
Market Grill was ok. I remember two of the steak dishes were good. The chicken was alright. The pork was too dry.
Fuego had the best service out of all the restaurants. Food was good too, just portions are little smaller than we expected.
Mole's food was so-so. Maybe it was my mistake ordering duck confit from a restaurant that's service contemporary Mexican. I remember one of the appetizers was extremely salty.

Service: Poor
We got attitude from the guy who checked us in. He forgot to give us towel keys. Didn't get the king size bed or the crib we requested. We had to request twice for a baby crib with their concierge. They gave us a Graco pack n play, which is fine. Another couple we met said they first delivered a tiny crib and they had to ask for another. Their cleaning staff was quite aggressive with wanting to clean our rooms.  Their cleaning schedule happened to conflict with my infant's nap and even after leaving the sign for them to not disturb, they would then call my room instead. The second day the cleaning staff came in they took all our dirty towels and didn't leave us any new ones. We had to call the concierge to ask them to bring us towels. I wouldn't trust their cleaning if I were you. They didn't change our bedsheets once while we were there, just made our beds.
Their waitstaff in general are pretty slow and need to be asked several times to do something. We asked about 3x for a high chair and was brought one with a broken strap. We gave up on asking for high chairs and just brought our own booster.
The concierge doesn't break bills for you, so either bring a lot of ones and fives or be prepared to awkwardly ask the waitstaff to break bills for you.
There's a towel hut near the kids pools and it seems like they're always out of towels by 4pm

Overall: For that amount of money, I expected more.  Won't be going back again.

reviews.author: Brandon Schlagel
reviews.text: Food was OK but not great, the buffet never changes. The room was decent, the jacuzzi on the patio needed work and they should invest in covers. The service was good overall. The pool and beach areas were both really nice.

reviews.author: Desh Hindle
reviews.text: This is a 3-star resort pretending to be a 5-star resort.  The food is very inconsistent (some reasonably good and some inexcusably terrible).  We watched a hot bar staff grab handfuls of pasta with bare hands and put it into serving dishes.  The room had some items either broken or not working, and the floor was never cleaned (though the other aspects of room cleaning was good).  Some of the staff was very nice, and others dismissive.  The pool lounge chairs have only one position and are extremely uncomfortable.  The pools were also very crowded, and certainly not peaceful with loud music booming at all hours it seemed.  There were ceiling water leaks in a couple places that created slipping hazards that seemed to be ignored by staff.  We did enjoy the beach, though there was a lot of seaweed much of the time.  There were some fun entertainment options and trips available.  All in all, fair to middling and not what we expected for the money.

reviews.author: Tony Summers
reviews.text:
Maybe our expectations were too high, we were very disappointed in the royal service. We only saw our butler twice during the 7 days we were there and were not told of a way to contact him.
Reception staff were rude, dismissive and unhelpful, with the exception of the two ladies that were very professional.
The pool and restaurant staff were very good.
The room was very tired and in need of an update, even though we were supposedly upgraded.
Rainwater pouring in through the ceiling continuously was dangerous and the subsequent towels left all over the floors made it even worse.
Not what you would expect from a luxury hotel.

reviews.author: Daniel Romero
reviews.text:
The hotel itself and its facilities is great. Perhaps my only "complaint" is the huge distance and stairs you need to walk just to go across the street. So, no issues here.

This isn't really an "All inclusive" hotel, there should be a category for "many/most things included" but not all. This is the case.

Service, is when things start to go south. Hotel staff is very friendly and house keeping and waiters are very helpful and kind. But there are things just unforgivable for a hotel of that is supposed to be one of the best. First, service pretty much shuts down after 10pm. I think there is only 1 restaurant open. My flight came in late (it's schedule at that time) and no more valet nor bell boys were available to help with luggage. These services should be 24 hours at a hotel like this. Then, front desk... I get it, but still, I asked the guy to open up a credit for me at the hotel for incidentals and he said it wasn't necessary, everything would be charged to my hotel room. Next day, I go and get a bed at the beach and guess what "your credit is not yet open". Next, my concierge never introduced herself to me, I was the one who had to find her, out of pure luck. I did find her only after I had talked to another concierge that wasn't assigned to me. So when I spoke to my correct concierge, I think she didn't like the fact that I spoke to another concierge first and she asked several questions about the offers that had already been presented to me. I noticed at the end, she secretly recorded everything I said in her celphone without my knowledge. I didn't say anything bad or made a big deal out of it. I just thought it was pretty awkward to be recorded without my knowledge at least.

Information provided about spa services was incomplete. I showed up with my wife unprepared (because I didn't get the info from the concierge) and had to miss about 15 minutes of my session, just because I had to go back to my room to get all that was needed.

I also had an altercation with one of the kids club guys. It didn't escalate, but I just never understood what his problem was if I said it was ok for them to charge me if I showed up 5 minutes late to pick up my kid. If you allow kids to be picked up late at a rate of 25 USD per hour and I said that's OK, I don't see why anyone we keep bugging me about not being late "otherwise it's 25 USD". If you don't do late pickups, just say so and I'll be on time, but don't bother me if I'm paying for the service.

Finally, Medical attention. There is Dr that I tried to go see because I was feeling pretty badly in the last few days. For Mexican standars this is expensive, although I admit considering I paid 50 USD for an Ibuprofen and Paracetamol small boxes, 120 USD per DR apointment sounds ok. Anyway, I stayed at the DRs office for over 40 minutes, nobody was there, nobody showed up, nobody answered the door. Had to go back to my room.

So, beautiful place, good location, nice staff but, more comprehensive services are far from perfect. Diefinitely not worth 5 stars. IMO.

UPDATE to "Guest service center management": you might wanna start feeling less proud and start doing more to give your guests their money's worth.

reviews.author: Janet Bogard
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful and could be cleaner not horrible dirty I did see 2 roaches one in the hallway by our room door and the other discuss me crawling near the baskets of bread at the buffet this hotel is eco friendly So be prepared to be extremely HOT!!!!! And Sweat Alot!!! Due to no air conditioning in the common areas Another Bigger Problem is the Food in every area all the restaurants & Buffet and room service is Horrible I mean Horrible be prepared to eat the pizza by the pool area it's ok not great but ok Also the pool has some black mold around the steps it wasn't the cleanest for the price this place is way over rated the people working are the most kindest humble loving & caring  most Awesome Attentive People I have ever met❤️ the view to the ocean is magnificent we made the best of our vacation and enjoy for the most part I did lose 11 pounds due to the horrible food Cancun is Beautiful But I would not stay here ever again I would like to visit the Hard Rock Cancun I talked to other people traveling home and they had good things to say about the food and hotel overall.

reviews.author: mary
reviews.text:
Good stay overall, not great.  Stayed the week between Christmas and New Years.
Pros:
Check-in was quick and easy.
Wait staff was very pleasant, with the exception of one waiter who was extremely rude.  We tipped the staff daily (a few dollars) and they seemed very appreciative.
Room was spacious and clean, although you could tell they were older.
Beautiful beach, plenty of space.
Most of the buffet food was good, restaurants were OK.
Drinks were good, not watered down.
Gym was decent.
Loved all the plants in each building, very green.

Cons:
I was under the impression there were Jacuzzi's near the pool - however they are not heated, only had jets.
Pool water was freezing!  I don't mind a refreshing pool, but this was extremely cold.  Everyone was shivering at the pool bar.
Restaurants fill up quickly, so if you forget to call a day in advance expect to eat at the buffet or eat late.
Room service menu is very limited, with no healthy options.
Lack of on-site activities.  Esp at night - no live music and the "show" was in one of the bars with very limited seating.
House keeping forgot to give us towels and took a while to bring them when requested.
Our fridge was not working in our room (and I had medication that needed to be kept cold). They brought another one, which was also not working and when I called, they said that the temperature was not supposed to be that cold even though i explained that it seemed like it was not on.  They finally brought a third fridge the next day, which worked!
Ice machine in our building was not working.  It took quite a while to have ice delivered. We set a standing ice delivery and they forgot the first one, but remembered the rest.

I would mostly likely not stay here again when comparing to other all-inclusive resorts I've stayed.  The lack of evening entertainment was really a bummer.

reviews.author: Amy Rosenberg
reviews.text:
There are good and bad things about this resort.  I'll start with the good.  First, the staff - we were extremely impressed with almost all of the staff we interacted with. Our assigned concierge, Juan Carlos, was wonderful to work with and so extremely helpful. We really enjoyed the staff in the hotel restaurants and out at the beach - they were almost all so very friendly and helpful. We had just a few rare negative experiences with staff, which I'll address under the appropriate areas with my negative comments, below.  Second, the beauty of the interior public spaces - the atriums are lush with vines and string lights hanging down. And there is a great area in a lobby bar area with daybeds, which was perfect for lounging and reading books on the one rainy day we had during our stay.  Third, location - it's a relatively quick ride from the airport, and about a 30 minute cab ride into downtown Cancun (depending on traffic). Finally -the ocean view - we had a beautiful ocean view from our room. I've attached some photos.

Now, the negatives. I'll start with the hard sell to join the Melia Circle program.  We reluctantly agreed to listen to a presentation on joining the Circle Program, which is basically a membership that allows you to stay at Melia properties around the world at discounted prices, for a yearly fee.  Some of the staff are VERY persistent about trying to get you to attend this presentation. Our concierge, Juan Carlos, did not unduly pressure us to attend a presentation, but did nicely ask us if we would, and he explained that he would receive some type of credit if we attended.  We really liked Juan Carlos a lot, so we agreed to attend for his sake. Other staff, however, would aggressively approach us and ask us to attend - even if we told that that we were already working with Juan Carlos.  One woman was irritatingly persistent, insisting that we needed to attend that day, after we told her repeatedly that we were on our way out of the hotel for a day trip to Isla Mujeres - she kept trying to get us to change our plans for the day. It was unpleasant. Then, on the day of our scheduled presentation, I tested positive for COVID, and thus was not planning to go anywhere beyond my hotel room.  The staff doing the presentation were irritated that I could not attend EVEN THOUGH I HAD COVID. They seemed to prioritize their sales pitch over public safety (and my own health and comfort - as though I'd actually want to attend an hour long sales pitch when I was as sick as a dog).

Second - the food & drinks.  Now, perhaps some of this was caused by my COVID infection (and a resulting effect on the taste buds), but even before I got sick, I felt like most of the  food in the hotel restaurants had little flavor.  It all seemed mediocre.  And drinks all seemed very watered down . The juices served during breakfast tasted like juice mixed with water. And mixed drinks from the bars tasted  mostly like watered-down mixers.  Also, once I got COVID, my boyfriend occasionally encountered some resistance from restaurant staff about sending food up to the room.

Third - the noise. This is a huge resort with hundreds of guests and a lot going on. It's not a particularly quiet, relaxing place.  We rented a cabana on the beach once day, which seemed like a nice luxurious indulgence, until the techno music started blasting. My boyfriend went to ask at some point if they could lower the volume, and they replied that most people like it louder.  Personally, I'd prefer the sound of the wind and the waves when trying to relax on the beach.

Fourth, the room was just okay.  We had a balcony but no deck furniture. We took the desk chairs from inside the room out to the balcony so that we could sit out there. Also, I only realized on the last day that our room was supposed to have a coffee maker (we had none)

Finally, housekeeping was inconsistent in replenishing our towels (mostly they seemed really stingy with washcloths, usually not giving us new ones even when they provided new bath towels).

reviews.author: Marc Sarhaddi
reviews.text:
Overall was good. However, you pay for a 5 star hotel, but it's more 3.5 or max 4 star hotel.
The rooms in tower 3 and 4 are not good. If you are not their VIP memebr, then you don't have access to their best services.
Food is good! Their asian restaurant is very good! I totally recommend it.

reviews.author: Jessica Nguyen
reviews.text:
We have been traveling to Mexico for summer vacations since 2012, so we've experienced several resorts in Playa Del Carmen, Playa Mujeres, and Cancun.  This was our first time at this resort and we had a group of 20 people.
Hotel: Very beautiful with lots of vegetation, but we wish it was better air-conditioned.  Most restaurants/shops/bars are in the main building (#3).  Check-in process could have been better. We upgraded to The Reserve and upon arrival had to check-in at a different location.  The employee just pointed us into the direction we needed to go, but should have actually walked us to the check-in desk because it's hidden and very confusing to find. The spa here is really nice and definitely worth it.
Rooms: Our room was in building 3 and we had a view of the main pool and ocean with a large balcony.  Very spacious for our family of 4 and I especially appreciated the privacy between the bathroom/shower and toilet area. AC in the rooms were horrible. We had our AC on 65, but room stayed at 71.
Restaurants: Most restaurants required reservations, and we are fortunate that some were able to accommodate our large group.  Malva Food Bazaar was their buffet restaurant. Great food options! They required temp check, masks, and gloves.  Blue Agave was their street tacos restaurant and was really good.  La Palapa is an outdoor restaurant for adults only that upgraded to The Reserve.  Great food also! Their green juice was delicious for breakfast and their shrimp we ordered for lunch was great! Cappella is their Italian restaurant. Most of their food was good and some family went twice, but we ordered their chicken dish and didn't enjoy the sauce at all. Enso was another great restaurant.  It's their Japanese restaurant and we really enjoyed their super fresh sushi and sashimi.  It's outdoors, and can get extremely hot if you're not seated around the outside perimeter.  There's no air flow in the middle of the restaurant, so be careful of that.  Fuego was not a good experience for us.  It's outdoors.  During the day, it's extra seating for the buffet, but at dinner, it's a separate restaurant.  We ate here our first night and service was slow, it was super hot, and the food wasn't even that great. We didn't try Mole, but one couple who was with us did and said it wasn't very good, so we didn't try it.  SAL Steak Cave is not included, but it was pretty good.  I was a little frustrated that some foods at all restaurants were considered upsells, and not included. This is something I've never experienced at any other resort.  So, we also won't be back because of this.  Lobster/steak/oysters should be included...not upsells.  Room service food was horrible, except for chicken strips and wasn't included for anyone not part of The Reserve. Poolside food and service was pretty great and there were lots of options for food around the pool.
Pools/Beach: This was one of the good experiences for us during our stay.  They have about 5 different pool sections that span across the entire resort and they all vary in depth.  The Reserve section was very quiet with several cabana beds.  Then there was a family pool that was right outside the buffet restaurant, the main pool, a lazy river, and a kiddie area.  We spent pretty much everyday in the pools and really enjoyed the poolside food/drink service.  The only downside was having to put our name on a list a day before to reserve cabanas, and even once you're on the list, you have to check-in between 9-11am to claim your cabana.  Pool chairs also had to be claimed by 7am every morning.  This process was definitely annoying and there would be times where people would steal chairs.  The beach was nice, but waves were too rough to swim safely and so we didn't get to enjoy the beach as much.
Overall, we had a great time and it truly is a nice resort, but  with all of the things we usually prefer, this resort was lacking, so we won't be back.

reviews.author: jcoakley
reviews.text: Nice hotel and good service, the weather didn't cooperate while we were here but we made the best of it. The food was ok, thought it would of been a little better for the price but I generally think the food tastes different in Mexico than America. Liquor was good they didn't have top shelf but I don't drink that most of the time anyways. The spa and other amenities were all good, can't say I'll be rushing back but it was better than the last place I stayed.

reviews.author: Karin E
reviews.text: My husband and I decided to come to Paradisus because we have a three years old son. It was told to us how good it is for kids. Indeed, there is the kids zone and babies zone. But it lacks  in others aspects. The room service is horrible, I ordered mac and cheese to my son, that arrived only on the following day. Actually, I don't understand how come they don't have a kids menu in room service? They also should offer at the buffet area foods for kids, like chicken fingers, clean pasta, mac and cheese and chicken nuggets (a good one, not like the one they served us yesterday at the kid's pool). So, this place is good but it could be better. The service needs more training and please, have some food for kids!

Currently staying at the Paradisus Cancun until saturday.
The hotel public areas, location and beach are amazing 5/5.
We are a little disappointed with the food selection in the buffet compared to other all inclusives we traveled to in Mexico. We will be trying the restaurants tonight.

But the biggest disappointment was the room, we initially purchased the luxury junior suite(ocean view) decided to get an upgrade to get the jacuzzi on the balcony. They didn't let us know that the new room is not renovated, everything is pretty old and the jacuzzi itself we are not getting into, it's old and wasn't cleaned, full of bird poop and other debris, they could use covers. Toilet was not flushing.
We tried to get our old room back and they said it's no longer available, neither is it possible to get a reserve ocean view room or anything.
Basically paid 500$ for a downgraded old room. Pretty disappointing and we'll be looking for other hotels for our next visit.

reviews.author: Wade Ha
reviews.text:
It was a truly satisfying trip.

I would like to leave a few comments in the hope that Paradisus Cancun will become an even more famous and wonderful resort. I visited this place with a friend and stayed for four days.

Having traveled to Cancun about five times, I have stayed at everything from mid-range to the most expensive luxury resorts. Based on this experience, I compared Paradisus Cancun to other places.

1. System

Perhaps because the resort recently reopened, its systems are significantly lacking compared to other resorts. I stayed here on a weekday, and the experience of having to search for a restaurant that was fully booked because I could not make a reservation for dinner was not pleasant.

In particular, the fact that meal reservations and event attendance bookings cannot be made via the smartphone application was very inconvenient compared to other resorts. It was truly unpleasant to have to wait for over an hour at the concierge from the morning just to make a reservation for dinner.

2. Information

It was difficult to read the map, whether in the application or the catalog. I had to search for quite a while because I didn't know where or on which floor the restaurant was located, and it was difficult to find out when and where various events were being held. The information provided by the smartphone application was complex and difficult to view at a glance.

3. Food/Dessert

The quality of the food and desserts was excellent. The ingredients were fresh, and it did not feel like cheap ingredients were being used. You can usually tell immediately if cheap ingredients are being used for desserts, but these were incredibly delicious.

Room service was also very neat and delicious, so I was satisfied.

4. Staff

All the staff worked incredibly hard, to the point where they looked exhausted.

In particular:

Front Desk - Roberto: He was very responsible and instilled confidence.

KAO Bar - Salvador: He was friendly and brought joy to those waiting.

It was pitiful to see the staff responding kindly even when guests who couldn't get dinner reservations were making strong complaints (even though this wasn't the fault of either the guests or the staff).

5. Overall Review

Like me, people visit Paradisus Cancun to spend a lot of money on a vacation. While everyone has different expectations, I believe Paradisus Cancun pursues one single direction: customer satisfaction.

To become a resort that everyone wants to visit, improvements are needed in the areas that are currently problematic. I believe that with just a little more development, it could become the best resort.

The staff are truly doing their best, but it was disappointing that the resort's internal systems did not seem to be functioning 100%.

I don't usually write reviews like this, but I am leaving this one because I believe it could become perfect with just a few changes. If I have the opportunity to visit again, I hope the issues I pointed out have been improved to surprise me. I especially hope the resort continues to improve, for the sake of all the staff members who were so kind to me.

reviews.author: MÓNICA MORÁN
reviews.text:
The hotel is very nice, but it needs some cleaning and maintenance. The restaurant entrance process is very slow. Sometimes you have to wait in lines for 15 minutes. Although food is always available, you have to wait up to an hour to get into the only restaurant open from 4 to 6 p.m. Room service has a charge just to have it delivered, which I find inappropriate.
The service is divided: you either get someone who serves you very well or you get very bad service.
There aren't enough lounge chairs.

reviews.author: Imanol Santano
reviews.text: It's a great hotel, but there's a clear, huge difference between the services it offers, like restaurants and pools, and the rooms. The former are renovated and new, while the latter are completely neglected and poorly maintained. They advertise it as a junior suite, but it's just a regular hotel room; it's not a suite at all. The reception staff is unfriendly and doesn't make you feel like you're in a four-diamond hotel. We had a major problem, and it was guest services who helped us, not reception. Overall, given the wide range of quality hotels nearby, this one isn't worth it.

reviews.author: Pri Sommelier
reviews.text: What can I say about Paradisus (extra charge for The Reserve category)? We arrived on Sunday and left Saturday morning. Even on Sunday, when we arrived, the receptionists didn't know where to send us to eat. We had to rely on our own intuition to find somewhere to eat, since beach bars and restaurants close at 4 pm. We managed to get cold cuts and cheeses at the cafeteria. It's worth noting that we weren't offered any drinks or anything at reception. Monday morning wasn't any better. For breakfast at Sante, we ordered scrambled eggs, which arrived without bread because they were out. They didn't know how to fix it. Two days later, at another breakfast, the bread arrived, and 50 minutes later, the eggs (very disappointing). The sun loungers without shade at the pools or beach designated for The Reserve guests (not exclusive at all) were available. We learned from the assigned concierge that you only have two days during your entire stay to use the shaded loungers (again, very exclusive). It's worth mentioning that alcohol stops at 11 PM throughout the hotel, and the minibar only has beer. If you order wine, it's the same for the entire hotel, costs $9, and you won't have access to it in your room. The hotel is geared towards Americans; they always speak to you in English and provide better service if you speak English. None of the service staff seem to know the hotel's operating hours. Please don't use room service; it takes an hour and a half to get a burger and wings, and when you ask for ice, it never arrives. The restaurants are decent. Capella is bad (overcooked pasta and sour sauce), Agua Marina is okay (they take your food away before you finish, which makes it bad), Sante is decent for dinner, Sal is good if you like American-style meat (charred on the outside but cooked to perfection), Malva is acceptable for a buffet and has some highlights, although it's always packed. Mascalzone is decent for stone-baked pizza (they don't have calzones or mushrooms). The lemon fish sushi was forgettable, but the octopus was outstanding. The Flora was delicious, with good use of ingredients and friendly service. I especially appreciated the service from the gentleman at the Nespresso café in The Reserve area! In short, a beautifully decorated hotel with sublime architecture, terribly managed and forgettable for the price.

reviews.author: lorena lodeiro
reviews.text:
Good evening, I'm staying at the hotel right now, today is my first day.
I agree with Sebastián's opinion (below). I don't understand why an "all-inclusive" hotel doesn't offer "everything included." What do I mean by that? I've stayed at other hotel chains where I didn't have to pay extra for meat. I can't believe that I have to pay extra to go to two of their restaurants. I've never experienced this before. The same goes for the wines; only two are included, and they aren't the best.
The signage isn't good; finding the Flora restaurant was difficult. However, I can't say anything negative about the service; Cinthia and Fanny were excellent, and the food was exquisite. We booked the highest Meliá category, Paradisus, so I didn't expect these things to be excluded. The same goes for the sun loungers (I don't remember what they're called here); they cost extra, unlike the regular lounge chairs, which are included. It's a real shame, I didn't expect it to be like this.
The room we got was perfect, comfortable, and cool (thankfully). The Flora restaurant is hot. All areas close at 11 pm; if you want something to eat or drink after that time, it's room service. And depending on your room category, they might deliver two or three times.
The only thing open 24 hours is the coffee area, where they serve something sweet or a savory sandwich.

reviews.author: Hector Lozano
reviews.text:
We have been coming to this hotel for many years. Lately, we have noticed a difference in the quality of service. There are not enough staff to meet the demand from guests. Going to a hotel restaurant means having to wait a long time to be attended to, served, etc. In the pool area, there are not enough servers. Food is constantly running out at the basic stations around the pool. The Malva restaurant (buffet) has declined in food quality. There are long lines to be seated.
We are very disappointed with how the quality of service has declined at what used to be a great hotel.

reviews.author: César
reviews.text: "I DO NOT RECOMMEND THAT HOTEL." I stayed from March 28th to 31st, 2025, and my reservation, paid a month in advance, was for a Junior Suite with an OCEAN VIEW. Upon arrival, I was assigned a room on the ground floor with a view of a nearly two-meter-tall planter, with a patio (it can't really be called a balcony) with exposed plumbing and no chairs or table. When I complained to the staff, they told me that the hotel has that floor and those rooms listed as having an ocean view, that the planters are for hurricane protection, and that they were currently fully booked. They said they could move me to another floor the following day, provided there was availability. When I requested a full refund of my reservation or a proportional refund for the room, they refused, arguing that since it was booked through an agency, I had to complain to them. The facilities are very nice, as are the beach and pools; the bar staff and some waiters are not rude but not friendly either.

reviews.author: YOLY AM
reviews.text:
My expectations were high, and to my taste, it left much to be desired. I think they have a lot of room for improvement in terms of value for money. The only redeeming feature of my stay was the Aguamarina restaurant; the service was excellent, especially from Renan, who was very attentive, helpful, friendly, and fun.

Thank you, Renan, for your attention and good humor.

reviews.author: Elenice Teixeira
reviews.text:
Excellent work by the recreation staff, special mention to Uriel's attentiveness and friendliness. Friendly with everyone, adults and children.
My reservation regarding the hotel services is that we paid for all-inclusive, but there are exceptions for everything: drinks, chairs on the beach and by the pool. The waiters only pay attention if you tip them; otherwise, they won't even come near you.

reviews.author: Rodrigo Rotenberg
reviews.text:
Disappointing Resort Experience – Distorted Priorities

Today, Thursday, September 26th, I'm in a cabana by the pool, right in front of the Água Marina restaurant. It's 10 am, the sun is strong, but the cabana should protect us and guarantee a moment of comfort and rest.

However, to my surprise, a hotel employee just removed the side curtains of the cabana, claiming they needed washing. The result? We were completely exposed to the sun. Is it really necessary to do this kind of maintenance in the middle of the morning, when guests are using the space?

It seems that, for the hotel, keeping a curtain shining is more important than preserving the comfort and experience of its customers. It's frustrating to realize that operational convenience has been prioritized over the needs of those paying for a relaxing and enjoyable experience.

Small details like this make all the difference in the guest experience and deserve to be reconsidered to improve the quality of service.

reviews.author: Biani Salas Morales
reviews.text: The Lemon Fish restaurant was the best of all; my waiters, Jorge and Arce (on two different days), gave me five-star service. The hotel staff in general are very friendly and make you feel at home. It's a shame that the hotel facilities are so run down and that there are leaks everywhere. The rooms have furniture from the 80s, and the bathrooms are practically unusable.

reviews.author: Valerie canuel
reviews.text:
We're currently staying at the Paradisus Cancun. It's an old but clean hotel. The service is very good.
It's difficult to get chairs on the beach if you don't book early in the morning. Our room was never cleaned by the housekeeper all week. The shower leaks under the sink; the room is nothing like a 5-star hotel. We found a cockroach in the room. The food is good, and the staff are generally very friendly. But I can't compare it to the other Paradisus hotels we've stayed at.

reviews.author: Daniel Serrano
reviews.text: Jesús Canche from the Capela restaurant was very attentive and always made sure our visit was pleasant. His service was excellent, but the food left much to be desired; it was a big disappointment.

reviews.author: Rocio Sanchez
reviews.text: It seems I got off on the wrong foot. I didn't feel as well taken care of as I have in other 5-star hotels I've stayed in. The facilities are very nice, but the staff service isn't very good. At the buffet, they don't even come near you to offer a glass of water, and don't even think about taking your food to your room, even if you have small children, because it's not allowed. I find it absurd. Also, not all the bars are open, including the lobby bar, which is one of the most important bars in a hotel. You have to reserve the daily specials, and you can't always find a spot. I really haven't felt comfortable.

reviews.author: Denisse Salazar
reviews.text: The location is super good, close to the shopping malls, aquarium etc. The atmosphere is a bit neglected, there are no signs so I got lost every day of my stay, the rooms are unclean, they don't sweep them, they only change the towels, so if you have sand on your clothes make sure you shake it off outside your room, the buffet food is the same, I didn't eat there the last 2 days because the taste had me sick, there was nothing that caught my attention, the dinner on the beach at the event was delicious, a steak with cream cheese risotto, I loved it!

reviews.author: Eloísa Cruz Rivas
reviews.text: The hotel service is very good overall, including room service, but especially the Malva Restaurant area, where the buffet offers a wide variety of foods for a light breakfast with cereal, fruit, salads, and much more! Excellent service from the young Enrique García, who is always attentive to all diners, whether foreign or Mexican. The service at the reservation restaurants is equally superb! I highly recommend eating at the Salt Restaurant! They have very special cuts of meat, excellent service with minimal wait times, and the restaurant itself is lovely!

reviews.author: Giselle Martínez
reviews.text:
I'll start by acknowledging the positive aspects of Paradisus.

The hotel's architecture is STUNNING, absolutely nothing bad to say about it. Every corner is spectacular.

The same goes for the staff and their service—a warm, family-like atmosphere, like being at home. If you see a staff member walking down the hallway, they'll ask about your day and how it's going. At the Malva restaurant, we received excellent service, especially from Mr. Alberto, and we were very grateful and happy thanks to him. We also received exceptional service at the coffee shop from a young man who, please excuse us for not knowing his name, but during our pleasant conversation, we forgot about that small detail. That, at least for us, is a huge plus. As for the kindness area, the staff were incredibly attentive, friendly, helpful, and fun. A big thank you to Irlanda, Gove, Azul, Nani, Monse, and Yami 🫶🏻

As for the negative aspects, which are of utmost importance to us, we left quite disappointed; It's their food.
Most of the time we ate at Malva.
The low quality and lack of care and hygiene are noticeable. It's always cold (except for the soups and creams), tastes bad, or is often from previous days. At Blue Agave, we literally ordered four tacos and it took 30 minutes to serve them.
We were there on a day of emergency due to Hurricane Berly, and for safety reasons, the convention area was set up for food consumption. That's where we confirmed the poor hygiene, as small cockroaches were crawling on the bread boxes (bread that's always exposed to the open air). Again, I have nothing bad to say about the service and attention from the staff, but the food left much to be desired. We had stomach problems every day and had to go out to find somewhere to eat. This, along with the fact that it's very hot and humid inside the hotel, makes us want to look for other options for our next visit.

reviews.author: Carolina Dosdoglirian
reviews.text:
We stayed at the hotel for a few days!
It's very nice, but I had been there a few years ago and the quality has gone down considerably. We weren't completely convinced.

I want to highlight Jorge's service at the Lima Fish restaurant; we had an amazing meal and he gave us great advice.

Also, Laura's beach service was fantastic—she was wonderful, bringing us food and being incredibly friendly.

Management should modernize or hire more staff; there are queues for breakfast and coffee, and the Italian restaurant is a rather unattractive section of the buffet.

reviews.author: Emiliano Ariel Torcal
reviews.text: My partner and I stayed here less than a month ago. The staff was very friendly, but the service left something to be desired. The information they provided was either scarce or incorrect; we had several instances where the staff told us one thing and then said another. The room was nice but had several flaws. The air conditioning was very noisy, the light switches had strange combinations, there were only four outlets in the entire room—two in the bathroom (which didn't work) and two on the sofa, none near the bed, and the curtain rods weren't attached to the curtains and were useless. Overall, a mediocre experience, with some good points and some not so good.

reviews.author: Sam
reviews.text:
It was a pleasant experience, but there were a lot of things I had to complain about, and I complained to guest service.

First of all, my flight arrived at 8:00 AM and I got to the hotel almost at 9:00 AM. The kids had their baths and everything, but the water wouldn't drain. The toilet was clogged, and we called someone to fix it. It took an hour, and they wouldn't give us another room until the next day. The internet was down for almost a day; the door was broken, and we couldn't get in. I had to wait until noon for them to change the battery outside the room, with the kids already asleep. The drinks are served in plastic cups—awful! Imagine seeing a margarita presented like that. Also, if you didn't get to the beach early to grab a chair or something to sit on, you had to stand or sit on the sand. On the last day, I went to the hotel's taco stand, and the waiter saw us when we raised our hands, but they didn't serve us. The glasses we requested were missing, and the waiter noticed but never provided them. Our chips and guacamole arrived 20 minutes later, while the next table that arrived after us was served much faster. The waiter was giving us strange looks. Room service was completely unhelpful and refused to apologize; we had to call the manager.

I don't recommend this place if you're staying in Cancun.

reviews.author: Cristian Vargas Avilés
reviews.text:
The hotel is very well renovated, quite pleasing to the eye, and when you arrive, you get the impression that it's a super luxurious hotel and that the service is going to be incredible, BUT, the truth is, it's not.
The rooms are quite rustic. The shower water spills out because the curtain is too short. There's also no non-slip mat. There's no notebook or pen for notes. The furniture is old, and the drawers are falling apart.
The service at the pool is quite poor. There are almost no waiters, and those who are there are reluctant to approach. The bartenders are rude and seem bothered by making drinks.
There aren't enough umbrellas, much less lounge chairs; everything is occupied by 8 a.m. They have plenty of Balinese beds, which cost exorbitantly $250 a day.

reviews.author: Gisele Naves
reviews.text: When we chose this "luxurious" hotel, it was initially because we thought it would be a good place to go with the family; we have a 2-year-old and 7-month-old daughter, and she is our priority. The cost-benefit ratio it offered seemed attractive. There were three of us: me, my husband, and our daughter. But right from the start, at reception for check-in, the reception area was crowded and very hot, and the people there, except for the baggage handlers, weren't very friendly and seemed quite eager to "get rid of us." Anyway, some things about the hotel were explained to us since we booked the "all-inclusive" package. When we went to the room, the first unpleasant thing was that I was surprised by someone who was going to clean the room. We had just arrived, we were taking a shower, and he simply opened the door to clean a room that was theoretically already clean. It wasn't his mistake, of course, but the hotel's, since the room was reserved for that day and time. Also, the room we booked had a view of the lagoon, but in reality, it only had a view of one end of the lagoon, haha. When we went to the pool, the only time we received quick and good service was when we sat facing the sea at one of the overpriced kiosks they try to rent you. Around the pool there are few kiosks and "free" spaces, so why do they try to sell you these overpriced ones? It's ridiculous. Oh, and those places were always empty. The waitresses had a sour face and were unwilling to help from beginning to end, except for one named Hugo who was always kind. Of course, the service is very different when you offer a tip, but you hotel managers and employees can't forget that kindness and politeness are not a differentiator, but an obligation. They try to sell you everything there, and they are insistent. The restaurants, even when empty, require reservations, except for two that were very crowded and had queues, but they are better than some of the others. I was pleasantly surprised by the Enzo Asian restaurant and especially the waiter José. The best in my opinion. The noise at night is excessive and continues all night. I made a complaint about the noise, but it didn't help at all. And to top it all off, on the last day the maid didn't provide face towels; something was missing every day. But here's a tip: Cancun is wonderful and worth visiting, I just don't recommend this hotel. I don't recommend it because for what it offers (treatment, politeness, respect, food, all-inclusive which doesn't seem all-inclusive to me) it's not worth it.
